sentences.zh: 資治通-{鑑}-第081巻

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 081
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 81

sentences.zh: 【晉紀三】起上章困敦，盡著雍涒灘，凡九年。

translations.literal: [Records of Jin, Number Three] Beginning from Shangzhang Kundun and extending through Zhuanyong Tuantan—nine years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Records of Jin, Number Three] Spanning from the cyclical year Shangzhang Kundun through Zhuanyong Tuantan—nine years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，呉大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, Wu proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Wu issued a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 杜預向江陵，王渾出橫江，攻呉鎭、戍，所向皆克。

translations.literal: Du Yu advanced toward Jiangling; Wang Hun marched out from Hengjiang and attacked Wu garrisons and outposts, conquering wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu marched on Jiangling while Wang Hun advanced from Hengjiang against Wu garrisons and outposts, capturing every objective he reached.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊午，王濬、唐彬撃破丹楊監盛紀。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wuwu, Wang Jun and Tang Bin defeated Sheng Ji, the Wu supervisor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuwu, Wang Jun and Tang Bin routed Sheng Ji, the Wu intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 呉人-{於}-江磧要害之處，-{並}-以鐵鎖橫截之；

translations.literal: The Wu forces at critical points along the river fords also stretched iron chains across to block passage;
translations.idiomatic: At strategic river fords the Wu forces had also stretched iron chains across the water to block the channel;

sentences.zh: 又作鐵錐，長丈-{餘}-，暗置江中，以逆拒舟艦。

translations.literal: They also made iron spikes more than one zhang long and secretly placed them in the river to obstruct ships.
translations.idiomatic: they also fashioned iron spikes more than ten feet long and set them hidden in the riverbed to impale incoming vessels.

sentences.zh: 濬作大筏數十，方百-{餘}-歩，縛草爲人，被甲持仗，令善水者以筏先行，遇鐵錐，錐輒著筏而去。

translations.literal: Wang Jun built several dozen large rafts, each more than a hundred paces square, bound straw into human figures, armored them and gave them weapons, and had skilled swimmers go ahead on the rafts; when they encountered iron spikes, the spikes would lodge in the rafts and be carried away.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun constructed dozens of large rafts a hundred paces or more on a side, fashioned straw effigies dressed in armor and bearing weapons, and sent skilled swimmers ahead on the rafts—when the spikes struck, they embedded in the rafts and were pulled free as the rafts passed.

sentences.zh: 又作大炬，長十-{餘}-丈，大數十圍，灌以麻油，在船前，遇鎖，然炬燒之，須臾，融液斷絶，-{於}-是船無所礙。

translations.literal: He also made great torches more than ten zhang long and several dozen wei in circumference, soaked them in sesame oil, and placed them at the prows; when they met the chains, they lit the torches to burn them, and in an instant the metal melted and broke apart, so the ships were unobstructed.
translations.idiomatic: He also built enormous torches more than ten zhang tall and several dozen wei around, soaked them in sesame oil, and mounted them on the prows—when they reached the chains, the torches were lit and burned through the iron until it melted and snapped, clearing the way for the fleet.

sentences.zh: 庚申，濬克西陵，殺呉都督留憲等。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Wang Jun captured Xiling and killed Liu Xian and other Wu commanders.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Wang Jun took Xiling and killed the Wu area commander Liu Xian and others.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，克荊門、夷道二城，殺夷道監陸晏。

translations.literal: On renxu, he captured the two cities of Jingmen and Yidao and killed Lu Yan, the Wu supervisor of Yidao.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, he captured Jingmen and Yidao and executed Lu Yan, the Wu intendant of Yidao.

sentences.zh: 杜預遣牙門周旨等帥奇兵八百泛舟夜渡江，襲樂鄕，多張旗幟，起火巴山。

translations.literal: Du Yu sent the gate officer Zhou Zhi and others leading eight hundred elite troops in boats to cross the river by night, raiding Lexiang, displaying many banners and setting fires on Mount Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu dispatched Zhou Zhi, a gate officer, with eight hundred picked troops in boats to cross the Yangtze by night and strike Lexiang, raising many banners and lighting fires on Mount Ba.

sentences.zh: 呉都督孫歆懼，與江陵督伍延書曰：「北來諸軍，乃飛渡江也。」

translations.literal: The Wu commander Sun Xin was alarmed and wrote to Wu Yan, the commander at Jiangling, saying, "The northern armies have flown across the river."
translations.idiomatic: The Wu area commander Sun Xin was terrified and wrote to Wu Yan, the Jiangling garrison commander: "The northern armies have flown across the river!"

sentences.zh: 旨等伏兵樂鄕城外，歆遣軍出拒王濬，大敗而還。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhi and the others lay in ambush outside Lexiang; Sun Xin sent troops out to oppose Wang Jun and was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhi's men lay in ambush outside Lexiang. Sun Xin sent troops to oppose Wang Jun and was driven back in defeat.

sentences.zh: 旨等-{發}-伏兵隨歆軍而入，歆不覺，直至帳下，虜歆而還。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhi and the others launched their ambush and entered along with Sun Xin's army; Sun Xin did not notice until they reached his headquarters, where they captured him and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhi then sprang his ambush and slipped in alongside Sun Xin's retreating force. Sun Xin never noticed until they were at his headquarters; they seized him and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 乙-{丑}-，王濬撃殺呉水軍都督陸景。

translations.literal: On yichou, Wang Jun attacked and killed Lu Jing, the Wu naval commander.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Wang Jun killed Lu Jing, the Wu commander of the navy.

sentences.zh: 杜預進攻江陵，甲戌，克之，斬伍延。

translations.literal: Du Yu pressed the attack on Jiangling; on jiaxu he captured it and executed Wu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu pressed the assault on Jiangling; on jiaxu he took the city and beheaded Wu Yan.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是沅、湘以南，接-{於}-交、廣，州郡皆望風送印綬。

translations.literal: Thereupon, south of the Yuan and Xiang rivers, connecting with Jiao and Guang, every province and commandery submitted seals and credentials at the first report of Jin arms.
translations.idiomatic: From that point south of the Yuan and Xiang, as far as Jiao and Guang, every province and commandery surrendered its seals and credentials at the first rumor of Jin advance.

sentences.zh: 預杖節稱詔而緩撫之。

translations.literal: Du Yu, bearing the staff of authority, proclaimed imperial edicts and treated them with lenient reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu carried the credential staff, issued proclamations in the emperor's name, and treated the surrendered territories with gentle reassurance.

sentences.zh: 凡所斬獲呉都督、監軍十四，牙門、郡守百二十-{餘}-人。

translations.literal: In all, they killed or captured fourteen Wu commanders and military supervisors, and more than 120 gate officers and prefectural administrators.
translations.idiomatic: In all they killed or captured fourteen Wu area commanders and army supervisors, along with more than 120 gate officers and prefectural administrators.

sentences.zh: 胡奮克江安。

translations.literal: Hu Fen captured Jiangan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fen captured Jiangan.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔：「王濬、唐彬旣定巴丘，與胡奮、王戎共平夏口、武昌，順流長騖，直造秣陵。

translations.literal: On yihai, an edict stated: "Now that Wang Jun and Tang Bin have secured Baling, together with Hu Fen and Wang Rong they shall pacify Xiakou and Wuchang, drive downstream at full speed, and press straight to Moling.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, an edict ordered: "Once Wang Jun and Tang Bin have secured Baling, they shall join Hu Fen and Wang Rong in taking Xiakou and Wuchang, then drive downstream at full speed straight for Moling.

sentences.zh: 杜預當鎭靜零、桂，懷輯衡陽。

translations.literal: Du Yu shall stabilize Ling and Gui and win over Hengyang with conciliation.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu is to pacify Ling and Gui and win over Hengyang through conciliation.

sentences.zh: 大兵旣過，荊州南境固當傳檄而定。

translations.literal: Once the main army has passed, the southern reaches of Jing Province should surely submit upon receiving proclamations alone.
translations.idiomatic: Once the main army has passed, the southern border of Jing Province should submit as soon as proclamations are sent out.

sentences.zh: 預等各分兵以益濬、彬，太尉充移屯項。」

translations.literal: Du Yu and the others shall each detach troops to reinforce Wang Jun and Tang Bin, and Grand Marshal Jia Chong shall move his headquarters to Xiang."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu and the others shall each detach troops to reinforce Wang Jun and Tang Bin, and Grand Marshal Jia Chong shall move his camp to Xiang."

sentences.zh: 王戎遣參軍襄陽羅尚、南陽劉喬將兵與王濬合攻武昌，呉江夏太守劉朗、督武昌諸軍虞昺皆降。

translations.literal: Wang Rong sent his staff officers Luo Shang of Xiangyang and Liu Qiao of Nanyang with troops to join Wang Jun in attacking Wuchang; Liu Lang, the Wu Administrator of Jiangxia, and Yu Bing, who commanded the Wuchang forces, both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong sent his staff officers Luo Shang of Xiangyang and Liu Qiao of Nanyang with troops to join Wang Jun in the assault on Wuchang; Liu Lang, Wu's administrator of Jiangxia, and Yu Bing, commander of the Wuchang garrison, both surrendered.

sentences.zh: 昺，翻之子也。

translations.literal: Yu Bing was the son of Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing was the son of Yu Fan.

sentences.zh: 杜預與衆軍會議，或曰：「百年之寇，未可盡克，方春水生，難-{於}-久駐，宜俟來冬，更爲大舉。」

translations.literal: Du Yu held a council with the various armies; some said, "This foe of a hundred years cannot yet be fully conquered; spring floods are rising and it will be hard to remain long—better to wait until next winter and launch a major campaign then."
translations.idiomatic: At a council of war Du Yu heard some officers argue: "A century-old enemy cannot be crushed in one stroke; the spring floods are rising and a prolonged stay will be difficult—we should wait until next winter and mount a major offensive then."

sentences.zh: 預曰：「昔樂毅藉濟西一戰以-{並}-強齊，今兵威已振，譬如破竹，數節之-{後}-，皆迎刃而解，無-{復}-著手處也。」

translations.literal: Du Yu said, "Long ago Yue Yi, with a single battle west of the Ji River, overthrew mighty Qi; now our military prestige is already soaring—it is like splitting bamboo: after the first few joints, every section after that splits open at a touch, with nothing left to resist."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu replied: "Long ago Yue Yi toppled mighty Qi with a single victory west of the Ji River. Our military prestige is already in full surge—breaking Wu now is like splitting bamboo: once the first few joints give way, every section after that falls apart at a touch, with nothing left to resist."

sentences.zh: 遂指授群帥方略，逕造建業。

translations.literal: He then instructed the commanders on strategy and pressed straight for Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately briefed his commanders on the plan and marched straight for Jianye.

sentences.zh: 呉主聞王渾南下，使丞相張悌督丹楊太守沈瑩、護軍孫震、副軍師諸葛靚帥衆三萬渡江逆戰。

translations.literal: When the Wu ruler heard that Wang Hun was advancing south, he sent Chancellor Zhang Ti to lead Danyang Administrator Shen Ying, Protector of the Army Sun Zhen, and Deputy Strategist Zhuge Jing with thirty thousand men across the river to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wu emperor learned that Wang Hun was marching south, he dispatched Chancellor Zhang Ti to lead Danyang Administrator Shen Ying, Protector of the Army Sun Zhen, and Deputy Strategist Zhuge Jing with thirty thousand men across the Yangtze to give battle.

sentences.zh: 至牛渚，沈瑩曰：「晉治水軍-{於}-蜀久矣，上流諸軍，素無戒備，名將皆死，幼少當任，恐不能-{御}-也。

translations.literal: When they reached Niuzhu, Shen Ying said, "Jin has been building a navy in Shu for a long time; the upper Yangtze garrisons have never been on guard, the famous generals are all dead, and young men hold the posts—I fear they cannot defend.
translations.idiomatic: At Niuzhu, Shen Ying said: "Jin has been building a navy in Shu for years. The upper Yangtze garrisons are unprepared, their famous generals are dead, and inexperienced young men hold command—I doubt they can hold the line.

sentences.zh: 晉之水軍必至-{於}-此，宜畜衆力以待其來，與之一戰，若幸而勝之，江西自淸。

translations.literal: Jin's navy is sure to reach this point; we should gather our full strength and wait for them to come, fight one decisive battle, and if we are fortunate enough to win, everything west of the river will be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's fleet is bound to reach us here. We should muster our full strength, wait for them to arrive, and fight one decisive battle—if we win, everything west of the river will be secure.

sentences.zh: 今渡江與晉大軍戰，不幸而敗，則大事去矣！」

translations.literal: If we cross the river now to fight Jin's main army and unhappily lose, then the great cause is lost!"
translations.idiomatic: But if we cross the river now to fight Jin's main force and lose, everything is lost!"

sentences.zh: 悌曰：「呉之將亡，賢愚所知，非今日也。

translations.literal: Zhang Ti said, "That Wu is about to perish is known to wise and foolish alike—it is not something that began today.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ti replied: "That Wu is doomed is plain to wise and foolish alike—it is nothing new.

sentences.zh: 吾恐蜀兵至此，衆心駭懼，不可-{復}-整。

translations.literal: I fear that when the Shu troops reach here, the army's hearts will be struck with terror and cannot be rallied again.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that when the Shu troops arrive, morale will collapse beyond recovery.

sentences.zh: 及今渡江，猶可決戰。

translations.literal: If we cross the river now, we can still fight a decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the river now, we can still fight a decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 若其敗喪，同死社稷，無所-{復}-恨。

translations.literal: If we are defeated, we die together for the state and have no further regret.
translations.idiomatic: If we are defeated, we die together for the realm—and have no regrets.

sentences.zh: 若其克捷，北敵奔走，兵勢萬倍，便當乘勝南上，逆之中道，不憂不破也。

translations.literal: If we win, the northern enemy will flee and our military momentum will multiply ten thousandfold; we should then ride the victory south and intercept them midway—there is no worry that we will not break them.
translations.idiomatic: If we win, the northern enemy will flee and our momentum will multiply tenfold; we can then press south and intercept them mid-route—and they will surely break.

sentences.zh: 若如子計，恐士衆散盡，坐待敵到，君臣倶降，無-{復}-一人死難者，不亦辱乎！」

translations.literal: If we follow your plan, I fear the troops will scatter completely, we will sit waiting for the enemy to arrive, lord and ministers will all surrender together, and not one man will die in the state's cause—is that not a disgrace!"
translations.idiomatic: Follow your plan and the troops will scatter, we will sit passively awaiting the enemy, lord and ministers will surrender together, and not one man will die for the realm—is that not a disgrace!"

sentences.zh: 三月，悌等濟江，圍渾部將城陽都尉張喬-{於}-楊荷。

translations.literal: In the third month, Zhang Ti and the others crossed the river and besieged Zhang Qiao, a commandant of Chengyang under Wang Hun's command, at Yanghe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Zhang Ti and his force crossed the river and besieged Zhang Qiao, a commandant of Chengyang under Wang Hun, at Yanghe.

sentences.zh: 喬衆-{才}-七千，閉柵請降。

translations.literal: Zhang Qiao's force numbered only seven thousand; he closed his palisades and requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiao had only seven thousand men. He shut his palisades and asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 諸葛艦欲屠之，悌曰：「強敵在前，不宜先事其小，且殺降不祥。」

translations.literal: Zhuge Jing wanted to massacre them; Zhang Ti said, "A powerful foe lies ahead—we should not bother with a small force first, and killing those who surrender is ill-omened."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jing wanted to slaughter them. Zhang Ti said: "A powerful enemy lies ahead—we should not waste effort on a small force first, and killing men who surrender bodes ill."

sentences.zh: 靚曰：「此屬以救兵未至，少力不敵，故且偽降以緩我，非眞伏也。

translations.literal: Zhuge Jing said, "These men, because relief has not yet arrived and their strength is too small to resist, are only pretending to surrender to delay us—they are not truly submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jing said: "These men are feigning surrender only because reinforcements have not arrived and they are too weak to fight—not because they truly submit.

sentences.zh: 若-{捨}-之而前，必爲-{後}-患。」

translations.literal: If we leave them and advance, they will surely become a threat from the rear."
translations.idiomatic: Leave them behind and advance, and they will surely become a threat in our rear."

sentences.zh: 悌不從，撫之而進。

translations.literal: Zhang Ti would not listen; he reassured them and marched on.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ti refused to listen, reassured them, and marched on.

sentences.zh: 悌與揚州刺史汝南周浚，結陳相對，沈瑩帥丹楊鋭卒、刀楯五千，三-{沖}-晉兵，不動。

translations.literal: Zhang Ti and Zhou Jun, the Inspector of Yang Province from Runan, deployed their battle lines facing each other; Shen Ying led five thousand crack troops from Danyang with swords and shields in three charges against the Jin army without budging it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ti and Zhou Jun, inspector of Yang Province from Runan, drew up their battle lines facing each other. Shen Ying led five thousand crack Danyang troops with swords and shields in three charges against the Jin lines without moving them.

sentences.zh: 瑩引退，其衆亂；

translations.literal: Shen Ying withdrew, and his troops fell into disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ying pulled back, and his troops fell into disorder;

sentences.zh: 將軍薛勝、蔣班因其亂而乘之，呉兵以次奔潰，將帥不能止，張喬自-{後}-撃之，大敗呉兵-{於}-版橋。

translations.literal: Generals Xue Sheng and Jiang Ban exploited the disorder and pressed the attack; Wu troops routed in succession and their commanders could not stop them; Zhang Qiao struck from the rear, and the Wu army was utterly defeated at Banqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Xue Sheng and Jiang Ban seized on the chaos and pressed the attack. Wu soldiers broke and fled in waves while their commanders could not halt the rout; Zhang Qiao then struck from the rear, crushing the Wu army at Banqiao.

sentences.zh: 諸葛靚帥數百人遁去，使過迎張悌，悌不肯去，靚自往牽之曰：「存亡自有大數，非卿一人所支，奈何故自取死！」

translations.literal: Zhuge Jing fled with several hundred men and sent someone to fetch Zhang Ti; Zhang Ti refused to leave. Zhuge Jing went himself, took hold of him, and said, "Survival and death follow a greater fate—not one man alone can sustain it; why deliberately seek your own death!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jing escaped with several hundred men and sent someone to bring Zhang Ti away. Zhang Ti refused to leave. Zhuge Jing went to him in person, took his arm, and pleaded: "Survival and death are governed by fate—not one man's shoulders alone. Why deliberately seek death!"

sentences.zh: 悌垂涕曰：「仲思，今日是我死日也！

translations.literal: Zhang Ti, weeping, said, "Zhongsi, today is my day to die!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ti wept: "Zhongsi, today is my day to die!

sentences.zh: 且我爲兒童時，便爲卿家丞相所識拔，常恐不得其死，負名賢知顧。

translations.literal: Moreover, when I was a child your family's chancellor singled me out; I have always feared that I would not die as I ought and would fail those great men who noticed me.
translations.idiomatic: Since I was a boy your family's chancellor singled me out. I have always feared dying unworthily and failing the great men who noticed me.

sentences.zh: 今以身徇社稷，-{復}-何道邪！」

translations.literal: Now I give my body for the altars of state—what other path is there!"
translations.idiomatic: Now I give my body for the realm—what other course is there!"

sentences.zh: 靚再三牽之，不動，乃流涙放去，行百-{餘}-歩，顧之，已爲晉兵所殺，-{並}-斬孫震、沈瑩等七千八百級，呉人大震。

translations.literal: Zhuge Jing tugged at him again and again without moving him, then wept and let him go; after walking more than a hundred paces he looked back and saw that Zhang Ti had already been killed by Jin troops; they also killed Sun Zhen, Shen Ying, and others—7,800 heads in all—and Wu was deeply shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jing pulled at him again and again, but Zhang Ti would not budge. Weeping, he released him and walked on. After a hundred paces he looked back—Zhang Ti had already been slain by Jin troops. Sun Zhen, Shen Ying, and others were also killed—7,800 heads in all—and Wu was shaken to its core.

sentences.zh: 初，詔書使王濬下建平，受杜預節度，至建業，受王渾節度。

translations.literal: Initially, the edict ordered Wang Jun to descend from Jianping under Du Yu's command, and upon reaching Jianye to come under Wang Hun's command.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the imperial edict had placed Wang Jun, descending from Jianping, under Du Yu's command until Jianye, and thereafter under Wang Hun's command.

sentences.zh: 預至江陵，謂諸將曰：「若濬得建平，則順流長驅，威名已著，不宜令受-{制}--{於}-我；

translations.literal: When Du Yu reached Jiangling, he told the generals, "If Wang Jun captures Jianping, he will drive downstream at full speed and his prestige will already be established—it is not fitting to have him constrained by us;
translations.idiomatic: When Du Yu reached Jiangling, he told his generals: "If Wang Jun takes Jianping, he will sweep downstream with his fame already established—it is not fitting to constrain him under our command;

sentences.zh: 若不能克，則無縁得施節度。」

translations.literal: if he cannot capture it, then there is no grounds for us to exercise command over him."
translations.idiomatic: if he cannot take it, we have no grounds to command him in the first place."

sentences.zh: 濬至西陵，預與之書曰：「足下旣摧其西籓，便當逕取建業，討累世之逋寇，釋呉人-{於}-塗炭，振旅還都，亦曠世一事也！」

translations.literal: When Wang Jun reached Xiling, Du Yu wrote to him, saying, "Now that you have broken their western defenses, you should press straight for Jianye, punish the rebel of generations, free the Wu people from misery, and return in triumph to the capital—that would be a deed for the ages!"
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun reached Xiling, Du Yu wrote him: "You have already shattered their western defenses—press straight for Jianye, destroy the rebel of generations, free the Wu people from misery, and return in triumph to the capital. That would be a deed for the ages!"

sentences.zh: 濬大悅，表呈預書。

translations.literal: Wang Jun was greatly pleased and forwarded Du Yu's letter in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun was delighted and forwarded Du Yu's letter in a memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 及張悌敗死，揚州別駕何惲謂周浚曰：「張悌舉全呉精兵殄滅-{於}-此，呉之朝野莫不震懾。

translations.literal: After Zhang Ti was defeated and killed, He Yun, the aide-de-camp of Yang Province, said to Zhou Jun, "Zhang Ti led all of Wu's elite troops to destruction here; court and country in Wu are all struck with terror.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Ti's defeat and death, He Yun, aide-de-camp of Yang Province, told Zhou Jun: "Zhang Ti led Wu's entire elite army to destruction here—court and country in Wu are terror-stricken.

sentences.zh: 今王龍驤旣破武昌，乘勝東下，所向輒克，土崩之勢見矣。

translations.literal: Now Wang Longxiang has already taken Wuchang and is advancing east on the momentum of victory, conquering wherever he goes—the signs of a realm collapsing are already visible.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Longxiang has already taken Wuchang and is advancing east on the tide of victory, capturing every objective—the realm is crumbling before our eyes.

sentences.zh: 謂宜速引兵渡江，直指建業，大軍猝至，奪其膽氣，可不戰禽也！」

translations.literal: I say we should quickly lead troops across the river and strike straight for Jianye; when the main army arrives suddenly and seizes their courage, we can capture them without a battle!"
translations.idiomatic: You should cross the river at once and strike straight for Jianye—the sudden arrival of the main army will paralyze them, and the city can be taken without a fight!"

sentences.zh: 浚善其謀，使白王渾。

translations.literal: Zhou Jun approved the plan and sent word to Wang Hun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jun approved the plan and reported it to Wang Hun.

sentences.zh: 惲曰：「渾暗-{於}-事機，而欲愼己免咎，必不我從。」

translations.literal: He Yun said, "Wang Hun is dull about opportunities and, wishing to protect himself from blame, will surely not follow us."
translations.idiomatic: He Yun said: "Wang Hun is dull about opportunities and, wanting to protect himself from blame, will surely refuse."

sentences.zh: 浚固使白之，渾果曰：「受詔但令屯江北以抗呉軍，不使輕進。

translations.literal: Zhou Jun still sent the report; Wang Hun indeed said, "I received orders only to hold north of the river against the Wu army—not to advance rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jun reported anyway. Wang Hun indeed replied: "My orders were only to hold north of the river against Wu—not to advance rashly.

sentences.zh: 貴州雖武，豈能獨平江東乎！

translations.literal: Even if our commander is brave, how can he alone pacify Jiangdong!
translations.idiomatic: Even if our commander is brave, how can he alone pacify all of Jiangdong!

sentences.zh: 今者違命，勝不足多，若其不勝，爲罪已重。

translations.literal: To disobey orders now—if we win, the merit is not great; if we lose, the guilt is already heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Disobey orders now and victory gains little credit, but defeat brings heavy blame.

sentences.zh: 且詔令龍驤受我節度，但當具君舟楫，一時倶濟耳。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the edict places Longxiang under my command—we need only prepare your boats and cross together at one time."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the edict places Longxiang under my command—we need only ready your boats and cross together."

sentences.zh: 惲曰：「龍驤克萬-{里}-之寇，以旣成之功來受節度，未之聞也。

translations.literal: He Yun said, "Longxiang conquering a foe ten thousand li away and then coming to accept command for work already accomplished—never have I heard of such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: He Yun said: "Longxiang has conquered an enemy ten thousand li away—never have I heard of a man who then came to take orders for a victory already won.

sentences.zh: 且明公爲上將，見可而進，豈得一一須詔令乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, my lord, as supreme commander, when you see an opportunity you advance—must you wait for an edict on every point!
translations.idiomatic: And you, my lord, are the supreme commander—when you see an opening you advance. Must you wait for an edict on every move!

sentences.zh: 今乘此渡江，十全必克，何疑何慮而淹留不進！

translations.literal: Cross the river on this opportunity and total victory is assured—what doubt, what hesitation keeps you lingering without advancing!
translations.idiomatic: Cross the river now and total victory is assured—what doubt or hesitation keeps you lingering here!

sentences.zh: 此鄙州上下所以恨恨也。」

translations.literal: This is why everyone in this province is filled with resentment."
translations.idiomatic: That is why everyone in this province seethes with frustration."

translations.literal: Wang Hun would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun would not listen.

sentences.zh: 王濬自武昌順流徑趣建業，呉主遣-{游}-撃將軍張象帥舟師萬人-{御}-之，像衆望旗而降。

translations.literal: Wang Jun sailed from Wuchang downstream straight for Jianye; the Wu ruler sent Strike General Zhang Xiang with ten thousand warships to oppose him, and Zhang Xiang's force surrendered at sight of the banners.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun sailed from Wuchang downstream straight for Jianye. The Wu emperor sent Strike General Zhang Xiang with ten thousand warships to oppose him—but Zhang Xiang's force surrendered at sight of the Jin banners.

sentences.zh: 濬兵甲滿江，旌旗燭天，威勢甚盛，呉人大懼。

translations.literal: Wang Jun's armored vessels filled the river, banners blazing to the sky; his power was very great, and the Wu people were deeply afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun's armored vessels filled the river, banners blazing across the sky. His might was overwhelming, and the people of Wu were terrified.

sentences.zh: 呉主之嬖臣岑昏，以傾險諛佞，致位九列，好興功役，爲衆患苦。

translations.literal: Chen Hun, a favorite of the Wu ruler, rose through treachery and flattery to one of the Nine Ministers; he loved launching public works and was a source of suffering for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hun, a favorite of the Wu emperor, had risen through treachery and flattery to one of the Nine Ministers. He loved launching wasteful public works and was a scourge to the people.

sentences.zh: 及晉兵將至，殿中親近數百人叩頭請-{於}-呉主曰：「北軍日近而兵不舉刃，陛下將如之何？」

translations.literal: When Jin troops were about to arrive, several hundred close attendants in the palace kowtowed and pleaded with the Wu ruler, saying, "The northern armies draw nearer daily yet our swords are not drawn—Your Majesty, what will you do?"
translations.idiomatic: As Jin troops drew near, several hundred palace attendants kowtowed before the Wu emperor: "The northern armies approach daily, yet our swords stay sheathed—Your Majesty, what will you do?"

sentences.zh: 呉主曰：「何故？」

translations.literal: The Wu ruler said, "For what reason?"
translations.idiomatic: The Wu emperor asked: "Why?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「正坐岑昏耳。」

translations.literal: They answered, "It is entirely because of Chen Hun."
translations.idiomatic: They answered: "It is all because of Chen Hun."

sentences.zh: 呉主獨言：「若爾，當以奴謝百姓！」

translations.literal: The Wu ruler said alone, "If that is so, I shall give up this slave to appease the people!"
translations.idiomatic: The Wu emperor said on his own: "If that is so, I shall give up this slave to appease the people!"

sentences.zh: 衆因曰：「唯！」

translations.literal: The crowd then said, "Yes!"
translations.idiomatic: The crowd shouted: "Yes!"

sentences.zh: 遂-{並}-起收昏。

translations.literal: They then rose together and seized Chen Hun.
translations.idiomatic: They rose together and seized Chen Hun.

sentences.zh: 呉主駱驛追止，已屠之矣。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler sent relay riders in haste to stop them, but Chen Hun had already been executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu emperor sent urgent riders to stop them—but Chen Hun had already been executed.

sentences.zh: 陶浚將討郭馬，至武昌，聞晉兵大入，引兵東還。

translations.literal: Tao Jun was about to campaign against Guo Ma; when he reached Wuchang and heard that Jin troops had invaded in force, he turned his army east.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Jun had been marching against Guo Ma. When he reached Wuchang and heard that Jin had invaded in force, he turned his army east.

sentences.zh: 至建業，呉主引見，問水軍消息，對曰：「蜀船皆小，今得二萬兵，乘大船以戰，自足破之。」

translations.literal: When he reached Jianye, the Wu ruler summoned him and asked about the navy; he answered, "The Shu ships are all small; now with twenty thousand troops aboard large vessels to fight, we can surely break them."
translations.idiomatic: At Jianye the Wu emperor received him and asked about the navy. Tao Jun replied: "The Shu ships are all small. Give me twenty thousand men aboard large vessels and we can surely defeat them."

sentences.zh: -{於}-是合衆，授浚節鉞。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wu mustered the forces and granted Tao Jun the battle-axe and credentials of command.
translations.idiomatic: Wu mustered its forces and granted Tao Jun the battle-axe and command credentials.

sentences.zh: 明日當-{發}-，其夜，衆悉逃潰。

translations.literal: They were to set out the next day; that night, the troops all fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: They were to depart the next day—but that night the troops all fled and scattered.

sentences.zh: 時王渾、王濬及琅邪王伷皆臨近境，呉司徒何植、建威將軍孫晏悉送印節詣渾降。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Hun, Wang Jun, and Sima You, Prince of Langya, were all near the border; Wu Minister of Works He Zhi and General Who Establishes Might Sun Yan all sent their seals and credentials to Wang Hun to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun, Wang Jun, and Sima You, Prince of Langya, were all near the border. Wu's Minister of Works He Zhi and General Who Establishes Might Sun Yan sent their seals and credentials to Wang Hun to surrender.

sentences.zh: 呉主用光祿勳薛瑩、中書令胡-{沖}-等計，分遣使者奉書-{於}-渾、灘、伷以請降。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler adopted the plan of Palace Grandee Xue Ying, Director of the Palace Secretariat Hu Chong, and others, dispatching envoys separately with letters to Wang Hun, Wang Jun, and Sima You to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu emperor adopted a plan from Palace Grandee Xue Ying, Director of the Palace Secretariat Hu Chong, and others, sending separate envoys with letters to Wang Hun, Wang Jun, and Sima You to sue for surrender.

sentences.zh: 又遺其群臣書，深自咎責，且曰：「今大晉平治四海，是英俊展節之秋，勿以移朝改朔，用損厥-{志}-。」

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to his officials, deeply blaming himself, and said, "Now Great Jin pacifies all within the four seas—this is the season for men of talent to display their loyalty; do not let the change of dynasty and calendar diminish your ambitions."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote his officials a letter of deep self-reproach, saying: "Great Jin now pacifies all under heaven—this is the season for talented men to serve. Do not let the change of dynasty dampen your ambitions."

sentences.zh: 使者先送璽綬-{於}-琅邪王伷。

translations.literal: The envoys first delivered the imperial seal and cordons to Sima You, Prince of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys first delivered the imperial seal and cordons to Sima You, Prince of Langya.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，王濬舟師過三山，王渾遣信要濬暫過論事；

translations.literal: On renyin, Wang Jun's fleet passed Sanshan; Wang Hun sent a message asking Wang Jun to stop briefly to discuss affairs;
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Wang Jun's fleet passed Sanshan. Wang Hun sent word asking Wang Jun to anchor briefly to confer;

sentences.zh: 濬舉帆直指建業，報曰：「風利，不得泊也。」

translations.literal: Wang Jun raised his sails and headed straight for Jianye, replying, "The wind is favorable—I cannot anchor."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun raised his sails and headed straight for Jianye, replying: "The wind is favorable—I cannot stop."

sentences.zh: 是日，濬戎卒八萬，方舟百-{里}-，鼓噪入-{於}-石頭，呉主皓-{面}-縛輿櫬，詣軍門降。

translations.literal: That day, Wang Jun's eighty thousand soldiers, with boats stretching a hundred li, shouting as they entered Shitou; the Wu ruler Sun Hao, bound and with a coffin on a cart, came to the camp gate to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Wang Jun's eighty thousand soldiers, in a fleet stretching a hundred li, shouting as they entered Shitou. The Wu emperor Sun Hao came to the camp gate bound, with a coffin on a cart, to surrender.

sentences.zh: 濬解縛焚櫬，延請相見。

translations.literal: Wang Jun untied him, burned the coffin, and invited him to meet.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun untied him, burned the coffin, and received him for an audience.

sentences.zh: 收其圖籍，克州四，郡四十三，戸五十二萬三千，兵二十三萬。

translations.literal: They collected maps and registers: four provinces conquered, forty-three commanderies, 523,000 households, and 230,000 troops.
translations.idiomatic: They collected the maps and registers—four provinces, forty-three commanderies, 523,000 households, and 230,000 troops.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞呉已平，群臣皆賀上壽。

translations.literal: When the court heard that Wu had been pacified, the ministers all congratulated the emperor on his longevity.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned that Wu had been pacified, the ministers all offered the emperor congratulations on his longevity.

sentences.zh: 帝執爵流涕曰：「此羊太傅之功也。」

translations.literal: The emperor, holding his cup, wept and said, "This is the achievement of Grand Tutor Yang."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, cup in hand, wept and said: "This is Grand Tutor Yang's achievement."

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍孫秀不賀，南向流涕曰：「昔討逆弱冠以一校尉創業，今-{後}-主舉江南而棄之，宗廟山陵，-{於}-此爲墟。

translations.literal: General of Agile Cavalry Sun Xiu did not offer congratulations; facing south he wept and said, "Long ago the Conqueror of Rebellion, in his early twenties, founded the enterprise from a single commandant's post; now the late ruler has surrendered all Jiangnan and abandoned it—the ancestral temples and imperial tombs are here reduced to ruins.
translations.idiomatic: General of Agile Cavalry Sun Xiu did not join the congratulations. Facing south, he wept and said: "Long ago the Conqueror of Rebellion, barely out of his teens, built an empire from a single commandant's post. Now the late ruler has surrendered all of Jiangnan and abandoned it—the ancestral temples and imperial tombs lie in ruins here.

sentences.zh: 悠悠蒼天，此何人哉！」

translations.literal: O vast blue Heaven—what manner of man is this!"
translations.idiomatic: O vast blue Heaven—what manner of man is this!"

sentences.zh: 呉之未下也，大臣皆以爲未可輕進，獨張華堅執以爲必克。

translations.literal: Before Wu had fallen, the ministers all held that one should not advance rashly; Zhang Hua alone steadfastly maintained that victory was certain.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wu fell, the ministers all argued against advancing rashly; Zhang Hua alone insisted that victory was certain.

sentences.zh: 賈充上表稱：「呉地未可悉定，方夏，江、淮下濕，疾疫必起，宜召諸軍還，以爲-{後}-圖。

translations.literal: Jia Chong submitted a memorial stating, "Wu cannot yet be fully pacified; it is now summer, and the Yangtze and Huai lowlands are damp—epidemics are sure to break out. The armies should be recalled and a plan made for later.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong submitted a memorial arguing: "Wu cannot yet be fully pacified. It is summer now, and the Yangtze and Huai lowlands are damp—epidemics are sure to break out. The armies should be recalled and a plan made for later.

sentences.zh: 雖腰斬張華不足以謝天下。」

translations.literal: Even if Zhang Hua were executed by waist severing, it would not suffice to appease the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Even executing Zhang Hua by waist severing would not suffice to appease the realm."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此是吾意，華但與吾同耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This is my own intent—Hua merely agrees with me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "This is my own intent—Hua merely agrees with me."

sentences.zh: 荀勗-{復}-奏，宜如充表，帝不從。

translations.literal: Xun Xu again memorialized that Jia Chong's proposal should be followed; the emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu memorialized again that Jia Chong's proposal should be adopted; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 杜預聞充奏乞罷兵，馳表固爭，使至轘轅而呉已降。

translations.literal: When Du Yu heard of Jia Chong's memorial requesting withdrawal of the armies, he sent an urgent memorial arguing forcefully; by the time the messenger reached Huanyuan, Wu had already surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Yu heard of Jia Chong's memorial requesting withdrawal, he sent an urgent counter-memorial—but by the time the messenger reached Huanyuan, Wu had already surrendered.

sentences.zh: 充慚懼，詣闕請罪，帝撫而不問。

translations.literal: Jia Chong, ashamed and afraid, went to the palace to confess his fault; the emperor comforted him and did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed and afraid, Jia Chong went to the palace to confess his fault. The emperor comforted him and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲申，詔賜孫皓爵歸命侯。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on jiashen, an edict enfeoffed Sun Hao as Marquis of Guiming.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on jiashen, an edict enfeoffed Sun Hao as Marquis of Guiming.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On yiyou, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, the court proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 大酺五日。

translations.literal: A grand feast was held for five days.
translations.idiomatic: A grand feast was held for five days.

sentences.zh: 遣使者分詣荊、揚撫慰，呉牧、守已下皆不更易，除其苛政，悉從簡易，呉人大悅。

translations.literal: Envoys were dispatched separately to Jing and Yang to offer reassurance; Wu prefects and administrators and all below were left unchanged, harsh policies were abolished, and everything was simplified—the people of Wu were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to Jing and Yang to offer reassurance. Wu prefects and administrators at every level were left in place, harsh policies were abolished, and governance was simplified—the people of Wu were overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 滕修討郭馬未克，聞晉伐呉，帥衆赴難，至巴丘，聞呉亡，縞素流涕，還，與廣州刺史閭-{豐}-、蒼梧太守王毅各送印綬請降。

translations.literal: Teng Xiu had been campaigning against Guo Ma without success; hearing that Jin was attacking Wu, he led his troops to the rescue. When he reached Baqiu and learned that Wu had perished, he wept in white mourning garb, returned, and together with Lu Feng, the Inspector of Guang Province, and Wang Yi, Administrator of Cangwu, each sent seals and credentials to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Xiu had been campaigning against Guo Ma without success. Hearing that Jin was attacking Wu, he marched to the rescue. At Baqiu he learned that Wu had fallen, wept in white mourning garb, and returned. He and Lu Feng, inspector of Guang Province, and Wang Yi, administrator of Cangwu, each sent their seals and credentials to surrender.

sentences.zh: 孫皓遣陶璜之子融持手書諭璜，璜流涕數日，亦送印綬降；

translations.literal: Sun Hao sent Tao Huang's son Rong with a personal letter to persuade Huang; Huang wept for several days and also sent his seals and credentials to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao sent Tao Huang's son Rong with a personal letter to persuade him. Huang wept for days, then sent his seals and credentials to surrender;

sentences.zh: 帝皆-{復}-其本職。

translations.literal: the emperor restored all of them to their original posts.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor restored all of them to their original posts.

sentences.zh: 王濬之東下也，呉城戍皆望風款附，獨建平太守吾彦嬰城不下，聞呉亡，乃降。

translations.literal: When Wang Jun marched east, Wu garrison cities all submitted at the first report of his approach; only Wu Yan, Administrator of Jianping, held his city and would not yield. When he heard that Wu had perished, he then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun marched east, Wu garrison cities surrendered at the first rumor of his approach. Only Wu Yan, administrator of Jianping, held his city and refused to yield. When he learned that Wu had fallen, he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 帝以彦爲金城太守。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Wu Yan Administrator of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Wu Yan administrator of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷尊寵孫秀、孫楷，欲以招來呉人。

translations.literal: Initially, the court honored and favored Sun Xiu and Sun Kai, intending thereby to win over the people of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the court had honored Sun Xiu and Sun Kai, hoping thereby to win over the people of Wu.

sentences.zh: 及呉亡，降秀爲伏波將軍，楷爲渡遼將軍。

translations.literal: When Wu fell, Sun Xiu was demoted to General Who Pacifies the Waves and Sun Kai to General Who Crosses the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu fell, Sun Xiu was demoted to General Who Pacifies the Waves and Sun Kai to General Who Crosses the Liao.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王伷遣使送孫皓及其宗族詣洛陽。

translations.literal: Sima You, Prince of Langya, sent envoys to escort Sun Hao and his clan to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima You, Prince of Langya, sent envoys to escort Sun Hao and his clan to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁亥朔，皓至，與其太子瑾等泥頭-{面}-縛，詣東陽門。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dinghai, the first day of the month, Sun Hao arrived; he and his crown prince Sun Jin and others came with mud on their heads and bound, to the Dongyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dinghai, the first day of the month, Sun Hao arrived. He and his crown prince Sun Jin and others came with heads covered in mud and faces bound, to the Dongyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 詔遣謁者解其縛，賜衣服、車乘、田三十頃，歳給錢-{谷}-、綿絹甚厚。

translations.literal: An edict sent a chamberlain to untie them and granted them clothing, carriages, thirty qing of farmland, and generous annual allotments of money, grain, silk, and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent a chamberlain to untie them and granted them clothing, carriages, thirty qing of farmland, and generous annual allotments of money, grain, silk, and brocade.

sentences.zh: 拜瑾爲中郎，諸子爲王者皆爲郎中，呉之舊望，隨-{才}-擢敘。

translations.literal: Sun Jin was appointed Palace Gentleman; all sons who had held royal titles were made Court Gentlemen; and eminent families of Wu were promoted according to their talents.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jin was appointed Palace Gentleman; all sons who had held royal titles were made Court Gentlemen; and eminent families of Wu were promoted according to their abilities.

sentences.zh: 孫氏將吏渡江者-{復}-十年，百姓-{復}-二十年。

translations.literal: Sun clan officers and officials who had crossed the Yangtze received ten years' tax exemption; the common people received twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Sun clan officers and officials who had crossed the Yangtze received ten years' tax exemption; commoners received twenty.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，帝臨軒，大會文武有位及四方使者，國子學生皆預焉。

translations.literal: On gengyin, the emperor appeared at the front hall and held a great assembly of civil and military officials with rank and envoys from all directions; students of the Imperial Academy all attended.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, the emperor held court and convened a great assembly of ranked civil and military officials and envoys from all directions; students of the Imperial Academy attended as well.

sentences.zh: 引見歸命侯皓及呉降人，皓登殿稽顙。

translations.literal: Sun Hao, Marquis of Guiming, and the Wu surrenderers were presented; Sun Hao ascended the hall and kowtowed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao, Marquis of Guiming, and the Wu surrenderers were presented. Sun Hao ascended the hall and kowtowed.

sentences.zh: 帝謂皓曰：「朕設此座以待卿久矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Sun Hao, "I have long set this seat waiting for you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Sun Hao: "I have long set this seat waiting for you."

sentences.zh: 皓曰：「臣-{於}-南方，亦設此座以待陛下。」

translations.literal: Sun Hao said, "Your subject, in the south, also set this seat waiting for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao replied: "Your subject, in the south, also set this seat waiting for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 賈充謂皓曰：「聞君在南方鑿人目，剝人-{面}-皮，此何等刑也？」

translations.literal: Jia Chong said to Sun Hao, "I hear that in the south you gouged out men's eyes and flayed men's faces—what sort of punishments are these?"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong said to Sun Hao: "I hear that in the south you gouged out men's eyes and flayed men's faces—what sort of punishments are these?"

sentences.zh: 皓曰：「人臣有弒其君及-{奸}-回不忠者，則加此刑耳。」

translations.literal: Sun Hao said, "When a subject murders his ruler or is treacherous and disloyal, then this punishment is applied."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao replied: "When a subject murders his ruler or proves treacherous and disloyal, then this punishment is applied."

sentences.zh: 充默然甚愧，而皓顏色無怍。

translations.literal: Jia Chong fell silent, deeply ashamed, while Sun Hao's expression showed no embarrassment.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong fell silent, deeply ashamed, while Sun Hao's expression showed not a trace of embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 帝從容問散騎常侍薛瑩孫皓所以亡，對曰：「皓暱近小人，刑罰放濫，大臣諸將，人不自保，此其所以亡也。」

translations.literal: The emperor casually asked Attendant Cavalier Xue Ying why Sun Hao's state had perished; he answered, "Sun Hao favored petty men, punishments were excessive, and ministers and generals could not protect themselves—this is why it perished."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor casually asked Attendant Cavalier Xue Ying why Sun Hao's state had fallen. He answered: "Sun Hao favored petty men, punishments ran wild, and ministers and generals could not protect themselves—that is why it fell."

sentences.zh: 它日，又問吾彦，對曰：「呉主英俊，宰輔賢明。」

translations.literal: On another day he asked Wu Yan, who answered, "The Wu ruler was talented and his chief ministers were wise."
translations.idiomatic: On another day he asked Wu Yan, who answered: "The Wu ruler was talented and his chief ministers were wise."

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「若是，何故亡？」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "If that is so, why did it perish?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed: "If that is so, why did it fall?"

sentences.zh: 彦曰：「天祿永終，-{歴}-數有屬，故爲陛下禽耳。」

translations.literal: Wu Yan said, "Heaven's mandate had run its course and the succession of dynasties had its appointed lord—therefore he was captured by Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan said: "Heaven's mandate had run its course and the succession of dynasties had its appointed lord—therefore he was captured by Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased with this answer.

sentences.zh: 王濬之入建業也，其明日，王渾乃濟江，以濬不待己至，先受孫皓降，意甚愧忿，將攻濬。

translations.literal: When Wang Jun entered Jianye, Wang Hun crossed the river only the next day; because Wang Jun had not waited for his arrival and had accepted Sun Hao's surrender first, Wang Hun was deeply ashamed and angry and was about to attack Wang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun entered Jianye; Wang Hun crossed the river only the next day. Because Wang Jun had not waited for him and had accepted Sun Hao's surrender first, Wang Hun was deeply ashamed and angry and was about to attack Wang Jun.

sentences.zh: 何攀勸濬送皓與渾，由是事得解。

translations.literal: He Pan urged Wang Jun to hand Sun Hao over to Wang Hun, and thereby the affair was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: He Pan urged Wang Jun to hand Sun Hao over to Wang Hun, and the affair was resolved.

sentences.zh: 何惲以渾與濬爭功，與周浚牋曰：「《書》貴克讓，《易》大謙光。

translations.literal: Because Wang Hun and Wang Jun were contending for credit, He Yun wrote to Zhou Jun, saying, "The Documents honors overcoming through forbearance; the Changes greatly exalts the light of humility.
translations.idiomatic: As Wang Hun and Wang Jun contended for credit, He Yun wrote to Zhou Jun: "The Documents honors overcoming through forbearance; the Changes greatly exalts the light of humility.

sentences.zh: 前破張悌，呉人失氣，龍驤因之，陷其區宇。

translations.literal: Earlier we broke Zhang Ti and the Wu people lost their spirit; Longxiang seized the opportunity and overran their territory.
translations.idiomatic: We broke Zhang Ti and the Wu people lost their spirit; Longxiang seized the opportunity and overran their territory.

sentences.zh: 論其前-{後}-，我實緩師，旣失機會，不及-{於}-事，而今方競其功；

translations.literal: Considering before and after, we in truth delayed our army, already missed the opportunity, and failed to achieve the result—yet now we are competing over credit;
translations.idiomatic: Before and after, we in truth delayed our army, missed the opportunity, and failed to finish the job—yet now we compete over credit;

sentences.zh: 彼旣不呑聲，將虧雍穆之弘，興矜爭之鄙，斯愚情之所不取也。」

translations.literal: if he will not swallow his voice, it will impair the magnanimity of harmony and breed the vulgarity of rivalry—this my foolish heart cannot accept."
translations.idiomatic: If he will not hold his tongue, it will impair the magnanimity of harmony and breed the vulgarity of rivalry—this my foolish heart cannot accept."

sentences.zh: 浚得牋，卽諫止渾。

translations.literal: Wang Jun received the letter and immediately admonished Wang Hun to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun received the letter and immediately admonished Wang Hun to desist.

sentences.zh: 渾不納，表濬違詔不受節度，誣以罪狀。

translations.literal: Wang Hun would not accept this and memorialized that Wang Jun had disobeyed the edict and refused command, fabricating charges against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun refused and memorialized that Wang Jun had disobeyed the edict and refused command, fabricating charges against him.

sentences.zh: 渾子濟，尚常山公主，宗黨強盛。

translations.literal: Wang Hun's son Wang Ji was married to the Princess of Changshan; their clan faction was powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun's son Wang Ji was married to the Princess of Changshan; their clan faction was powerful.

sentences.zh: 有司奏請檻車-{征}-濬，帝弗許，但以詔書責讓濬以不從渾命，違-{制}-昧利。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized requesting that Wang Jun be summoned in a prisoner cart; the emperor did not permit this, but merely sent an edict rebuking Wang Jun for not obeying Wang Hun's orders and violating regulations for private gain.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized requesting that Wang Jun be summoned in a prisoner cart. The emperor refused, but sent an edict rebuking Wang Jun for disobeying Wang Hun's orders and violating regulations for private gain.

sentences.zh: 濬上書自理曰：「前被詔書，令臣直造秣陵，又令受太尉充節度。

translations.literal: Wang Jun submitted a memorial in his own defense, saying, "Previously I received an edict ordering me to press straight to Moling, and also ordering me to accept Grand Marshal Jia Chong's command.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun submitted a memorial in his own defense: "Previously I received an edict ordering me to press straight to Moling, and also ordering me to accept Grand Marshal Jia Chong's command.

sentences.zh: 臣以十五日至三山，見渾軍在北岸，遣書邀臣；

translations.literal: I reached Sanshan on the fifteenth and saw Wang Hun's army on the north bank; he sent a letter inviting me;
translations.idiomatic: I reached Sanshan on the fifteenth and saw Wang Hun's army on the north bank; he sent a letter inviting me;

sentences.zh: 臣水軍風-{發}-乘勢，逕造賊城，無縁回船過渾。

translations.literal: my navy, with the wind at its back, rode the momentum straight to the rebel capital—there was no occasion to turn the ships back to visit Wang Hun.
translations.idiomatic: my navy, with the wind at its back, rode the momentum straight to the rebel capital—there was no occasion to turn back and visit Wang Hun.

sentences.zh: 臣以日中至秣陵，暮乃被渾所下當受節度之符，欲令臣明十六日悉將所領還圍石頭，又索蜀兵及鎭南諸軍人名定見。

translations.literal: I reached Moling at midday; only at evening did I receive from Wang Hun the credential ordering me to accept his command, requiring me on the sixteenth to lead all my forces back to besiege Shitou, and also demanding rosters of Shu troops and all southern garrison personnel.
translations.idiomatic: I reached Moling at midday; only at evening did I receive Wang Hun's credential ordering me to accept his command, requiring me on the sixteenth to lead all my forces back to besiege Shitou, and also demanding rosters of Shu troops and all southern garrison personnel.

sentences.zh: 臣以爲皓已來降，無縁空圍石頭；

translations.literal: I considered that Sun Hao had already come to surrender—there was no occasion to besiege Shitou for nothing;
translations.idiomatic: I considered that Sun Hao had already surrendered—there was no occasion to besiege Shitou for nothing;

sentences.zh: 又，兵人定見，不可倉猝得就，皆非當今之急，不可承用，非敢忽棄明-{制}-也。

translations.literal: moreover, troop rosters could not be produced on short notice; none of these were urgent matters of the moment and could not be complied with—I did not dare lightly disregard your clear orders.
translations.idiomatic: moreover, troop rosters could not be produced on short notice; none of these were urgent and could not be complied with—I did not dare lightly disregard clear orders.

sentences.zh: 皓衆叛親離，匹夫獨坐，雀鼠貪生，苟乞一活耳，而江北諸軍不知虚實，不早縛取，自爲小誤。

translations.literal: Sun Hao's followers had deserted him and his kin had abandoned him; he sat alone like a common man, clinging to life like a sparrow or rat, merely begging to survive—yet the armies north of the river, not knowing the true situation, failed to seize and bind him early; that was their own small error.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao's followers had deserted him and his kin had abandoned him; he sat alone, clinging to life like a sparrow or rat, merely begging to survive—yet the armies north of the river, not knowing the true situation, failed to seize him early. That was their own small error.

sentences.zh: 臣至便得，更見怨恚，-{並}--{云}-：『守賊百日，而令他人得之。』

translations.literal: I captured him as soon as I arrived, yet was met with resentment and anger, and they even said, 'We besieged the rebel for a hundred days, and let someone else take him.'
translations.idiomatic: I captured him as soon as I arrived, yet was met with resentment—and they even said: 'We besieged the rebel for a hundred days and let someone else take him.'

sentences.zh: 臣愚以爲事君之道，苟利社稷，死生以之。

translations.literal: I foolishly believe that the way of serving one's ruler is: if it benefits the altars of state, one stakes life and death upon it.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that the way of serving one's ruler is: if it benefits the realm, one stakes life and death upon it.

sentences.zh: 若其顧嫌疑以避咎責，此是人臣不忠之利，實非明主社稷之福也。」

translations.literal: If one looks to suspicions to avoid blame, that is the petty profit of a disloyal subject—it is truly not the blessing of a wise ruler and the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: If one looks to suspicions to avoid blame, that is the petty profit of a disloyal subject—it is no blessing to a wise ruler or the realm."

sentences.zh: 渾又騰周浚書-{云}-：「濬軍得呉寶物。」

translations.literal: Wang Hun also forwarded Zhou Jun's letter saying, "Wang Jun's army obtained Wu treasures."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun also forwarded Zhou Jun's letter saying: "Wang Jun's army obtained Wu treasures."

sentences.zh: 又-{云}-「濬牙門將李髙放火燒皓偽宮。」

translations.literal: He also said, "Wang Jun's gate officer Li Gao set fire and burned Sun Hao's false palace."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Wang Jun's gate officer Li Gao set fire and burned Sun Hao's palace."

sentences.zh: 濬-{復}-表曰：「臣孤根獨立，結恨強宗。

translations.literal: Wang Jun again memorialized, saying, "I stand alone with shallow roots and have made enemies of powerful clans.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun memorialized again: "I stand alone with shallow roots and have made enemies of powerful clans.

sentences.zh: 夫犯上-{干}-主，其罪可救；

translations.literal: Offending one's superiors and affronting the ruler—such crimes may be pardoned;
translations.idiomatic: Offending one's superiors and affronting the ruler—such crimes may be pardoned;

sentences.zh: 乖忤貴臣，禍在不測。

translations.literal: but crossing powerful ministers brings disaster beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: but crossing powerful ministers brings disaster beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 偽郎將孔攄説：去二月武昌失守，水軍行至，皓案行石頭還，左右人皆跳刀大呼-{云}-：『要當爲陛下一死戰決之。』

translations.literal: The false regime's Gentleman-Commandant Kong Shu reported: last second month, when Wuchang fell and the navy was approaching, Sun Hao was inspecting Shitou on his return; the men around him all drew swords and shouted, 'We must fight to the death for Your Majesty and settle this.'
translations.idiomatic: The former regime's Gentleman-Commandant Kong Shu reported: last second month, when Wuchang fell and the navy was approaching, Sun Hao was inspecting Shitou on his return; the men around him all drew swords and shouted: 'We must fight to the death for Your Majesty and settle this.'

sentences.zh: 皓意大喜，意必能然，便盡出金寶以賜與之。

translations.literal: Sun Hao was greatly pleased, believing it would surely come to pass, and distributed all his gold and treasures to them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao was greatly pleased, believing they would surely fight, and distributed all his gold and treasures to them.

sentences.zh: 小人無狀，得便持走。

translations.literal: The petty men, without restraint, seized the opportunity and ran off with the goods.
translations.idiomatic: The petty men seized the opportunity and ran off with the goods.

sentences.zh: 皓懼，乃圖降首。

translations.literal: Sun Hao was afraid and then planned to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao was terrified and then planned to surrender.

sentences.zh: 降使-{適}-去，左右劫奪財物，略取妻妾，放火燒宮。

translations.literal: When the surrender envoy had just departed, those around him plundered goods, seized wives and concubines, and set fire to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the surrender envoy had just departed, those around him plundered goods, seized wives and concubines, and set fire to the palace.

sentences.zh: 皓逃身竄首，恐不脱死。

translations.literal: Sun Hao hid himself in terror, fearing he would not escape death.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao hid himself in terror, fearing he would not escape death.

sentences.zh: 臣至，遣參軍主者救斷其火耳。

translations.literal: When I arrived, I sent my staff officer in charge to rescue and extinguish the fire—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: When I arrived, I sent my staff officer to rescue and extinguish the fire—that is all.

sentences.zh: 周浚先入皓宮，渾又先登皓舟，臣之入觀，皆在其-{後}-。

translations.literal: Zhou Jun entered Sun Hao's palace first; Wang Hun boarded Sun Hao's boat first—my entry to inspect came after both of them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jun entered Sun Hao's palace first; Wang Hun boarded Sun Hao's boat first—my entry came after both of them.

sentences.zh: 皓宮之中，乃無席可坐，若有遺寶，則浚與渾先得之矣。

translations.literal: Inside Sun Hao's palace there was not even a mat to sit on; if any treasures remained, Wang Jun and Wang Hun would have gotten them first.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Sun Hao's palace there was not even a mat to sit on; if any treasures remained, Wang Jun and Wang Hun would have gotten them first.

sentences.zh: 等-{雲}-臣屯聚蜀人，不時送皓，欲有反狀。

translations.literal: They also say I gathered Shu men and did not promptly deliver Sun Hao, intending rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: They also say I gathered Shu men and did not promptly deliver Sun Hao, intending rebellion.

sentences.zh: 又恐動呉人，言臣皆當誅殺，取其妻子，冀其作亂，得騁私忿。

translations.literal: They also alarm the people of Wu, saying I should all be executed and my wives and children taken, hoping they will rise in revolt so they can vent private grudges.
translations.idiomatic: They also alarm the people of Wu, saying my men should all be executed and their wives and children seized, hoping to provoke revolt so they can vent private grudges.

sentences.zh: 謀反大逆，尚以見加，其-{餘}-謗□沓，故其宜耳。

translations.literal: If even the capital charge of plotting rebellion is fabricated against me, the rest of the slander piled on is only to be expected.
translations.idiomatic: If even the capital charge of plotting rebellion is fabricated against me, the rest of the slander piled on is only to be expected.

sentences.zh: 今年平呉，誠爲大慶；

translations.literal: This year Wu was pacified—truly a great celebration;
translations.idiomatic: This year Wu was pacified—truly a great celebration;

sentences.zh: -{於}-臣之身，更受咎累。」

translations.literal: for my person, I receive blame and trouble instead."
translations.idiomatic: yet for my person, I receive blame and trouble instead."

sentences.zh: 濬至京師，有司奏濬違詔，大不敬，請付廷尉科罪；

translations.literal: When Wang Jun reached the capital, the relevant offices memorialized that he had disobeyed the edict—a grave disrespect—and requested he be handed to the Court of Justice for punishment;
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun reached the capital, the relevant offices memorialized that he had disobeyed the edict—a grave disrespect—and requested he be handed to the Court of Justice for punishment;

sentences.zh: 詔不許。

translations.literal: the edict did not permit this.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 又奏濬赦-{後}-燒賊船百三十五艘，輒敕付廷尉禁推；

translations.literal: They again memorialized that after the amnesty Wang Jun had burned 135 rebel ships and ordered this referred to the Court of Justice for investigation;
translations.idiomatic: They again memorialized that after the amnesty Wang Jun had burned 135 rebel ships and ordered this referred to the Court of Justice for investigation;

sentences.zh: 詔勿推。

translations.literal: the edict ordered that it not be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor ordered that it not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 渾、濬爭功不已，帝命守廷尉廣陵劉頌校其事，以渾爲上功，濬爲中功。

translations.literal: Wang Hun and Wang Jun continued contending over credit without end; the emperor ordered Liu Song of Guangling, Administrator of the Court of Justice, to adjudicate the matter, rating Wang Hun's merit as highest and Wang Jun's as middle.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun and Wang Jun continued contending over credit. The emperor ordered Liu Song of Guangling, administrator of the Court of Justice, to adjudicate, rating Wang Hun's merit as highest and Wang Jun's as middle.

sentences.zh: 帝以頌折法失理，左遷京兆太守。

translations.literal: The emperor, holding that Liu Song's application of the law was unreasonable, demoted him to Administrator of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, holding that Liu Song's application of the law was unreasonable, demoted him to administrator of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，增賈充邑八千戸，以王濬爲輔國大將軍，封襄陽縣侯；

translations.literal: On gengchen, Jia Chong's fief was increased by eight thousand households; Wang Jun was made General Who Assists the State and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangyang County;
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Jia Chong's fief was increased by eight thousand households; Wang Jun was made General Who Assists the State and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangyang County;

sentences.zh: 杜預爲當陽縣侯；

translations.literal: Du Yu was made Marquis of Dangyang County;
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu was made Marquis of Dangyang County;

sentences.zh: 王戎爲安-{豐}-縣侯；

translations.literal: Wang Rong was made Marquis of Anfeng County;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong was made Marquis of Anfeng County;

sentences.zh: 封琅邪王伷二子爲亭侯；

translations.literal: Sima You, Prince of Langya's two sons were enfeoffed as village marquises;
translations.idiomatic: two sons of Sima You, Prince of Langya, were enfeoffed as village marquises;

sentences.zh: 增京陵侯王渾邑八千戸，進爵爲公；

translations.literal: Marquis of Jingling Wang Hun's fief was increased by eight thousand households and his rank advanced to duke;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun, Marquis of Jingling, received an increase of eight thousand households and was advanced to duke;

sentences.zh: 尚書關内侯張華進封廣武縣侯，增邑萬戸；

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing and Marquis within the Passes Zhang Hua was advanced to Marquis of Guangwu County with an increase of ten thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua, Director of the Masters of Writing and Marquis within the Passes, was advanced to Marquis of Guangwu County with an increase of ten thousand households;

sentences.zh: 荀勗以專典詔命功，封一子爲亭侯；

translations.literal: Xun Xu, for his service in exclusively managing edicts, had one son enfeoffed as a village marquis;
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu, for his service in managing edicts, had one son enfeoffed as a village marquis;

sentences.zh: 其-{餘}-諸將及公卿以下，賞賜各有差。

translations.literal: the remaining generals and grandees and all below received rewards in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: the remaining generals, grandees, and all below received rewards in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 帝以平呉，策告羊祜廟，乃封其夫人夏侯氏爲萬歳鄕君，食邑五千戸。

translations.literal: Because Wu had been pacified, the emperor reported by written prayer at Yang Hu's temple and enfeoffed his wife Lady Xiahou as Village Lady of Wansui with a fief of five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wu had been pacified, the emperor reported by written prayer at Yang Hu's temple and enfeoffed his wife Lady Xiahou as Village Lady of Wansui with a fief of five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 王濬自以功大，而爲渾父子及黨與所挫抑，毎進見，陳其攻伐之勞及見枉之狀，或不勝忿憤，逕出不辭；

translations.literal: Wang Jun considered his achievement great, yet was suppressed by Wang Hun, his son, and their faction; each time he appeared at court he stated his labors in the campaign and the wrong done him, and sometimes, unable to contain his anger, he would leave directly without taking leave;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun considered his achievement great, yet was suppressed by Wang Hun, his son, and their faction. Each time he appeared at court he recounted his campaign labors and the wrong done him, and sometimes, unable to contain his anger, he would leave without taking leave;

sentences.zh: 帝毎容恕之。

translations.literal: the emperor each time tolerated and forgave him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor each time tolerated and forgave him.

sentences.zh: 益州護軍-{范}-通謂濬曰：「卿功則美矣，然恨所以居美者未盡善也。

translations.literal: Fan Tong, Protector of the Army in Yi Province, said to Wang Jun, "Your achievement is indeed splendid, yet I regret that the way you occupy that splendor is not entirely good.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tong, Protector of the Army in Yi Province, said to Wang Jun: "Your achievement is splendid, yet I regret that the way you occupy that splendor is not entirely wise.

sentences.zh: 卿旋旃之日，角巾私第，口不言平呉之事，若有問者，輒曰：『聖人之德，群帥之力，老夫何力之有！』

translations.literal: On the day you return with banners furled, wear a kerchief at your private residence and speak not of pacifying Wu; if anyone asks, simply say, 'It is the sage's virtue and the commanders' strength—what strength had this old man!'
translations.idiomatic: On the day you return with banners furled, wear a kerchief at your private residence and speak not of pacifying Wu. If anyone asks, simply say: 'It is the sage's virtue and the commanders' strength—what strength had this old man!'

sentences.zh: 此藺生所以屈廉頗也，王渾能無愧乎！」

translations.literal: This is how Lord Lin caused Lian Po to bow in shame—can Wang Hun fail to feel ashamed!"
translations.idiomatic: That is how Lord Lin humbled Lian Po—can Wang Hun fail to feel ashamed!"

sentences.zh: 濬曰：「吾始懲鄧艾之事，懼禍及身，不得無言；

translations.literal: Wang Jun said, "I began by taking warning from Deng Ai's fate, fearing disaster would reach my person—I could not remain silent;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun said: "I began by taking warning from Deng Ai's fate, fearing disaster would reach me—I could not remain silent;

sentences.zh: 其終不能遣諸胸中，是吾褊也。」

translations.literal: That in the end I cannot banish these things from my breast—this is my narrowness."
translations.idiomatic: That I could never banish these things from my breast—that was my own narrowness."

sentences.zh: 時人-{鹹}-以濬功重報輕，爲之憤邑。

translations.literal: People of the time all considered Wang Jun's achievement great and his reward slight, and were indignant on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time all felt Wang Jun's achievement was great and his reward too slight, and were indignant on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 博士秦秀等-{並}-上表訟濬之屈，帝乃遷濬鎭軍大將軍。

translations.literal: Erudite Qin Xiu and others all submitted memorials pleading Wang Jun's wrong; the emperor then promoted Wang Jun to General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Qin Xiu and others submitted memorials pleading Wang Jun's wrong. The emperor then promoted Wang Jun to General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 王渾嘗詣濬，濬嚴設備衞，然-{後}-見之。

translations.literal: Wang Hun once visited Wang Jun; Wang Jun set up strict guards and only then received him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun once visited Wang Jun, who set up strict guards and only then received him.

sentences.zh: 杜預還襄陽，以爲天下雖安，忘戰必危，乃勤-{於}-講武，申嚴戍守。

translations.literal: Du Yu returned to Xiangyang, holding that though the realm was at peace, forgetting war would surely bring danger; he therefore diligently trained troops and tightened garrison defense.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu returned to Xiangyang, believing that though the realm was at peace, forgetting war would surely bring danger. He diligently trained troops and tightened garrison defense.

sentences.zh: 又引滍、淯水以浸田萬-{餘}-頃，開揚口通零、桂之漕，公私賴之。

translations.literal: He also channeled the Zhi and Yu rivers to irrigate more than ten thousand qing of farmland, opened Yangkou to connect transport to Ling and Gui, and both public and private interests relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: He also channeled the Zhi and Yu rivers to irrigate more than ten thousand qing of farmland and opened Yangkou to connect transport to Ling and Gui—both public and private interests benefited.

sentences.zh: 預身不跨馬，射不穿札，而用兵-{制}-勝，諸將莫及。

translations.literal: Du Yu himself did not ride horses and could not pierce a writing slip with an arrow, yet in using troops to achieve victory none of the generals could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu himself did not ride horses and could not pierce a writing slip with an arrow, yet in military victory none of the generals could match him.

sentences.zh: 預在鎭，數餉遺洛中貴要；

translations.literal: While Du Yu was in his post, he repeatedly sent gifts to powerful figures in Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: While Du Yu held his post, he repeatedly sent gifts to powerful figures in Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 或問其故，預曰：「吾但恐爲害，不求益也。」

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, Du Yu said, "I only fear being harmed—I do not seek advantage."
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why, Du Yu said: "I only fear being harmed—I do not seek advantage."

sentences.zh: 王渾遷-{征}-東大將軍，-{復}-鎭壽陽。

translations.literal: Wang Hun was transferred to General Who Conquers the East and again garrisoned Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun was transferred to General Who Conquers the East and again garrisoned Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 諸葛靚逃竄不出。

translations.literal: Zhuge Jing fled and hid, not appearing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jing fled into hiding and would not appear.

sentences.zh: 帝與靚有舊，靚姊爲琅邪王妃，帝知靚在姊間，因就見焉。

translations.literal: The emperor had old ties with Zhuge Jing; Zhuge Jing's elder sister was the Princess of Langya, and knowing Zhuge Jing was staying with his sister, the emperor went there to see him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had old ties with Zhuge Jing. Zhuge Jing's elder sister was the Princess of Langya, and knowing he was staying with her, the emperor went to see him.

sentences.zh: 靚逃-{於}-廁，帝又逼見之，謂曰：「不謂今日-{復}-得相見！」

translations.literal: Zhuge Jing fled to the privy; the emperor pressed in to see him again and said, "I never thought we could meet again today!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jing fled to the privy. The emperor pressed in to see him again and said: "I never thought we could meet again today!"

sentences.zh: 靚流涕曰：「臣不能漆身皮-{面}-，-{復}-睹聖顏，誠爲慚恨！」

translations.literal: Zhuge Jing wept and said, "Your subject could not lacquer his body and flay his face, yet again behold the sage countenance—I am truly ashamed and regretful!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jing wept: "Your subject could not lacquer his body and flay his face, yet again behold the imperial countenance—I am truly ashamed!"

sentences.zh: 詔以爲侍中；

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Attendant-in-Ordinary;
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him Attendant-in-Ordinary;

sentences.zh: 固辭不拜，歸-{於}-鄕-{里}-，終身不向朝廷而坐。

translations.literal: he firmly declined and would not accept, returned to his home village, and throughout his life would not sit facing the direction of the court.
translations.idiomatic: he firmly declined, returned to his home village, and throughout his life would not sit facing the direction of the court.

sentences.zh: 六月，-{復}-封丹水侯睦爲髙陽王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Marquis of Danshui Sima Mu was again enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Marquis of Danshui Sima Mu was again enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，己未，封皇弟延祚爲樂平王，尋薨。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the eighth month, on jiwei, the emperor's younger brother Yanzuo was enfeoffed as Prince of Le Ping; soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, on jiwei, the emperor's younger brother Yanzuo was enfeoffed as Prince of Le Ping; soon after he died.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚寅，賈充等以天下一統，屢請封禪；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on gengyin, Jia Chong and others, because the realm was unified, repeatedly requested a fengshan sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengyin, Jia Chong and others, citing the unification of the realm, repeatedly requested a fengshan sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，前將軍靑州刺史淮南胡威卒。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, Hu Wei of Huainan, General of the Vanguard and Inspector of Qing Province, died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Hu Wei of Huainan, General of the Vanguard and inspector of Qing Province, died.

sentences.zh: 威爲尚書，嘗諫時政之寬。

translations.literal: When Hu Wei was Director of the Masters of Writing, he once remonstrated about the leniency of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Wei was Director of the Masters of Writing, he once remonstrated about the leniency of current policy.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「尚書郎以下，吾無所假借。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Below the rank of Masters of Writing Gentleman, I show no leniency."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Below the rank of Masters of Writing Gentleman, I show no leniency."

sentences.zh: 威曰：「臣之所陳，豈在丞、郎、令史，正謂如臣等輩，始可以肅化明法耳！」

translations.literal: Hu Wei said, "What your subject remonstrates about is not assistants, gentlemen, and clerks—it is precisely men like your subject who must first uphold rectification and clarify the law!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu Wei said: "What I remonstrate about is not assistants, gentlemen, and clerks—it is precisely men like me who must first uphold rectification and clarify the law!"

sentences.zh: 是歳，以司隸所統郡置司州，凡州十九，郡國一百七十三，戸二百四十五萬九千八百四十。

translations.literal: This year, the commanderies under the Metropolitan Governor were established as Si Province; in all there were nineteen provinces, 173 commanderies and kingdoms, and 2,459,840 households.
translations.idiomatic: This year the commanderies under the Metropolitan Governor were established as Si Province. In all there were nineteen provinces, 173 commanderies and kingdoms, and 2,459,840 households.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔自漢末，四海分崩，刺史内親民事，外領兵馬。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Since the end of Han, the four seas split apart; provincial inspectors handled civil affairs internally and commanded troops externally.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "Since the end of Han, the four seas split apart; provincial inspectors handled civil affairs internally and commanded troops externally.

sentences.zh: 今天下爲一，當韜戢-{干}-戈，刺史分職，皆如漢氏故事；

translations.literal: Now the realm is one; arms should be sheathed, and provincial inspectors should divide their duties according to Han precedent;
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is one; arms should be sheathed, and provincial inspectors should divide their duties according to Han precedent;

sentences.zh: 悉去州郡兵，大郡置武吏百人，小郡五十人。」

translations.literal: all provincial and commandery troops shall be abolished; large commanderies shall have a hundred military officers, small commanderies fifty."
translations.idiomatic: all provincial and commandery troops shall be abolished; large commanderies shall have a hundred military officers, small commanderies fifty."

sentences.zh: 交州牧陶璜上言：「交、廣州西數千-{里}-，不賓屬者六萬-{餘}-戸，至-{於}-服從官役，-{才}-五千-{餘}-家。

translations.literal: Tao Huang, Inspector of Jiao Province, submitted a statement: "Jiao and Guang provinces extend several thousand li to the west; more than sixty thousand households do not submit, and of those who perform official service there are only a little more than five thousand families.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Huang, inspector of Jiao Province, submitted a statement: "Jiao and Guang extend several thousand li to the west. More than sixty thousand households do not submit, and of those who perform official service there are only a little more than five thousand families.

sentences.zh: 二州脣齒，唯兵是鎭。

translations.literal: The two provinces are lip and teeth to each other—only troops can stabilize them.
translations.idiomatic: The two provinces depend on each other like lip and teeth—only troops can stabilize them.

sentences.zh: 又，-{寧}-州諸夷，接-{據}-上流，水陸-{並}-通，州兵未宜約損，以示單虚。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the various tribes of Ning Province hold the upper reaches; land and water routes both connect—provincial troops should not yet be reduced, lest we appear weak and empty."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the various tribes of Ning Province hold the upper reaches; land and water routes both connect—provincial troops should not yet be reduced, lest we appear weak and empty."

sentences.zh: -{僕}-射山濤亦言「不宜去州郡武備」。
