translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Shan Tao also said, "It is not fitting to remove provincial and commandery military defenses."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Shan Tao also said: "It is not fitting to remove provincial and commandery military defenses."

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及永-{寧}-以-{後}-，盜賊群起，州郡無備，不能禽-{制}-，天下遂大亂，如濤所言。

translations.literal: When the Yongning era came afterward, bandits rose in groups; provinces and commanderies had no defenses and could not capture and control them—the realm fell into great disorder, just as Shan Tao had said.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongning era that followed, bandits rose in groups. Provinces and commanderies had no defenses and could not suppress them—the realm fell into great disorder, just as Shan Tao had warned.

sentences.zh: 然其-{後}-刺史-{復}-兼兵民之政，州鎭愈重矣。

translations.literal: Yet afterward provincial inspectors again combined military and civil authority, and provincial garrisons grew ever heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Yet afterward provincial inspectors again combined military and civil authority, and provincial power grew ever heavier.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏以來，羌、胡、鮮卑降者，多處之塞内諸郡。

translations.literal: Since Han and Wei, surrendered Qiang, Hu, and Xianbei were mostly settled in commanderies within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Wei, surrendered Qiang, Hu, and Xianbei had mostly been settled in commanderies within the passes.

sentences.zh: 其-{後}-數因忿恨，殺害長吏，漸爲民患。

translations.literal: Afterward they repeatedly, out of resentment, killed senior officials and gradually became a scourge to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they repeatedly killed senior officials out of resentment and gradually became a scourge to the people.

sentences.zh: 侍-{御}-史西河郭欽上疎曰：「戎狄強獷，-{歴}-古爲患。

translations.literal: Attendant Censor Guo Qin of Xihe submitted a memorial, saying, "The Rong and Di are fierce and unruly—they have been a scourge through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Censor Guo Qin of Xihe submitted a memorial: "The Rong and Di are fierce and unruly—they have been a scourge through the ages.

sentences.zh: 魏初民少，西北諸郡，皆爲戎居，内及京兆、魏郡、弘農，往往有之。

translations.literal: In early Wei the population was small; northwestern commanderies were all settled by Rong, and even within, as far as Jingzhao, Wei Commandery, and Hongnong, they were often found.
translations.idiomatic: In early Wei the population was small; northwestern commanderies were all settled by Rong, and even within—as far as Jingzhao, Wei Commandery, and Hongnong—they were often found.

sentences.zh: 今雖服從，若百年之-{後}-有風塵之警，胡騎自平陽、上黨不三日而至孟津，北地、西河、太原、馮翊、安定、上郡盡爲狄庭矣。

translations.literal: Though they now submit, if a hundred years hence there is an alarm of war, Hu cavalry from Pingyang and Shangdang could reach Mengjin in less than three days—Beidi, Xihe, Taiyuan, Fufeng, Anding, and Shang Commandery would all become Di territory.
translations.idiomatic: Though they now submit, if a hundred years hence war breaks out, Hu cavalry from Pingyang and Shangdang could reach Mengjin in less than three days—Beidi, Xihe, Taiyuan, Fufeng, Anding, and Shang would all become Di territory.

sentences.zh: 宜及平呉之威，謀臣猛將之略，漸徙内郡雜胡-{於}-邊地，峻四夷出入之防，明先王荒服之-{制}-，此萬世之長策也。」

translations.literal: We should, while the prestige of pacifying Wu is still strong and with the strategists' and fierce generals' plans, gradually relocate the mixed Hu of inner commanderies to the borderlands, strengthen the defenses against the four barbarians' coming and going, and clarify the former kings' system of wild territories—this is a long-term strategy for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: While the prestige of pacifying Wu is still strong, we should use our strategists' and generals' plans to gradually relocate the mixed Hu of inner commanderies to the borderlands, strengthen defenses against barbarian incursions, and restore the former kings' system of wild territories—this is a strategy for ten thousand generations."

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 春，三月，詔選孫皓宮人五千人入宮。

translations.literal: In spring, in the third month, an edict selected five thousand of Sun Hao's palace women to enter the harem.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the third month, an edict selected five thousand of Sun Hao's palace women for the harem.

sentences.zh: 帝旣平呉，頗事-{游}-宴，怠-{於}-政事，掖庭殆將萬人。

translations.literal: Once the emperor had pacified Wu, he devoted himself considerably to pleasure banquets and neglected governance; the inner palace nearly reached ten thousand women.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wu was pacified, the emperor devoted himself to pleasure banquets and neglected governance; the inner palace nearly reached ten thousand women.

sentences.zh: 常乘羊車，恣其所之，至便宴寢；

translations.literal: He often rode in a goat cart, going wherever he pleased, and wherever he arrived he would feast and sleep;
translations.idiomatic: He often rode in a goat cart wherever he pleased, feasting and sleeping wherever he stopped;

sentences.zh: 宮人競以竹-{葉}-插戸，鹽汁灑地，以引帝車。

translations.literal: palace women competed to insert bamboo leaves in their doorways and sprinkle salt water on the ground to attract the emperor's cart.
translations.idiomatic: palace women competed to insert bamboo leaves in their doorways and sprinkle salt water on the ground to attract the emperor's cart.

sentences.zh: 而-{後}-父楊駿及弟珧、濟始用事，交通請謁，勢傾内外，時人謂之三楊，舊臣多被疎退。

translations.literal: Then the empress's father Yang Jun and his brothers Yang Yao and Yang Ji began to wield power, trading favors and petitions; their influence tilted inside and outside the court, and people of the time called them the Three Yang; many old ministers were sidelined.
translations.idiomatic: Then the empress's father Yang Jun and his brothers Yang Yao and Yang Ji began to wield power, trading favors and petitions. Their influence dominated court and country, and people called them the Three Yangs; many old ministers were sidelined.

sentences.zh: 山濤數有規諷，帝雖知而不能改。

translations.literal: Shan Tao repeatedly offered remonstrance and satire; though the emperor knew, he could not change.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao repeatedly offered remonstrance; though the emperor knew, he could not change.

sentences.zh: 初，鮮卑莫護跋始自塞外入居遼西棘城之北，號曰慕容部。

translations.literal: Initially, the Xianbei leader Mohuba first entered from beyond the passes to settle north of Jicheng in Liaoxi and was called the Murong tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the Xianbei leader Mohuba entered from beyond the passes to settle north of Jicheng in Liaoxi and was called the Murong tribe.

sentences.zh: 莫護跋生木延，木延生渉歸，遷-{於}-遼東之北。

translations.literal: Mohuba begot Muyan; Muyan begot Shegui, who moved to the north of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Mohuba begot Muyan; Muyan begot Shegui, who moved to the north of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 世附中國，數從-{征}-討有功，拜大單-{于}-。

translations.literal: For generations they attached themselves to China, repeatedly followed campaigns with merit, and were appointed Grand Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they attached themselves to China, repeatedly served in campaigns with merit, and were appointed Grand Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，渉歸始寇昌黎。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, Shegui first raided Changli.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Shegui first raided Changli.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬寅，髙平武公陳騫薨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on renyin, Chen Qian, Duke Wu of Gaoping, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renyin, Chen Qian, Duke Wu of Gaoping, died.

sentences.zh: 是歳，揚州刺史周浚移鎭秣陵。

translations.literal: This year, Zhou Jun, Inspector of Yang Province, moved his headquarters to Moling.
translations.idiomatic: This year Zhou Jun, inspector of Yang Province, moved his headquarters to Moling.

sentences.zh: 呉民之未服者，屢爲寇亂，浚皆討平之。

translations.literal: Wu people who had not yet submitted repeatedly caused bandit disturbances; Zhou Jun suppressed and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: Wu people who had not yet submitted repeatedly caused bandit disturbances; Zhou Jun suppressed them all.

sentences.zh: 賓禮故老，搜求俊乂，威惠-{並}-行，呉人悅服。

translations.literal: He treated elders with courtesy, sought out talented men, and combined authority with kindness—the people of Wu submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: He treated elders with courtesy, sought out talented men, and combined authority with kindness—the people of Wu submitted gladly.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁-{丑}-朔，帝親祀南郊。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on dingchou, the first day of the month, the emperor personally sacrificed at the Southern Altar.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on dingchou, the first day of the month, the emperor personally sacrificed at the Southern Altar.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，喟然問司隸校尉劉毅曰：「朕可方漢之何帝？」

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, he sighed and asked Liu Yi, Metropolitan Commandant, "To which Han emperor can I be compared?"
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were complete, he sighed and asked Liu Yi, metropolitan commandant: "To which Han emperor can I be compared?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「桓、靈。」

translations.literal: He answered, "Huan and Ling."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Huan and Ling."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何至-{於}-此？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "How could it come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "How could it come to that?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「桓、靈賣官錢入官庫，陛下賣官錢入私門。

translations.literal: He answered, "Huan and Ling's sale-of-office money went into the state treasury; Your Majesty's sale-of-office money goes into private hands.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Huan and Ling's sale-of-office money went into the state treasury; Your Majesty's goes into private hands.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，殆不如也！」

translations.literal: By this measure, you are probably worse!"
translations.idiomatic: By that measure, you are probably worse!"

sentences.zh: 帝大笑曰：「桓、靈之世，不聞此言，今朕有直臣，固爲勝之。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed loudly and said, "In the age of Huan and Ling one never heard such words—now I have a straight-speaking minister; I am surely better than they."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed loudly: "In the age of Huan and Ling one never heard such words—now I have a straight-speaking minister; I am surely better than they."

sentences.zh: 毅爲司隸，糾繩豪貴，無所顧忌。

translations.literal: As Metropolitan Commandant, Liu Yi investigated and restrained powerful nobles without regard for anyone.
translations.idiomatic: As metropolitan commandant, Liu Yi investigated and restrained powerful nobles without fear or favor.

sentences.zh: 皇太子鼓吹入東掖門，毅劾奏之。

translations.literal: When the crown prince's ceremonial musicians entered the Eastern Side Gate, Liu Yi impeached and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince's ceremonial musicians entered the Eastern Side Gate, Liu Yi impeached and reported it.

sentences.zh: 中護軍、散騎常侍羊琇，與帝有舊恩，典禁兵，豫機密十-{餘}-年，恃寵驕侈，數犯法。

translations.literal: Yang Xiu, Central Protector of the Army and Attendant Cavalier, had old favor with the emperor, commanded the palace guard, and participated in secrets for more than ten years; relying on favor he was arrogant and extravagant and repeatedly violated the law.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiu, Central Protector of the Army and Attendant Cavalier, had old favor with the emperor, commanded the palace guard, and participated in secrets for more than ten years. Relying on favor he was arrogant and extravagant and repeatedly violated the law.

sentences.zh: 毅劾奏琇罪當死；

translations.literal: Liu Yi impeached and reported that Yang Xiu's crime deserved death;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi impeached Yang Xiu, reporting that his crime deserved death;

sentences.zh: 帝遣齊王攸私請琇-{於}-毅，毅許之。

translations.literal: the emperor sent Prince of Qi Sima You to privately intercede for Yang Xiu with Liu Yi, and Liu Yi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor sent Prince of Qi Sima You to privately intercede for Yang Xiu with Liu Yi, and Liu Yi agreed.

sentences.zh: 都官從事廣平程衞徑馳入護軍營，收琇屬吏，考問陰私，先奏琇所犯狼籍，然-{後}-言-{於}-毅。

translations.literal: Cheng Wei of Guangping, an aide in the Capital Crimes Office, rode straight into the Protector of the Army's camp, seized Yang Xiu's subordinate officials, interrogated their private affairs, first reported Yang Xiu's crimes in detail, and only then spoke to Liu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wei of Guangping, an aide in the Capital Crimes Office, rode straight into the Protector of the Army's camp, seized Yang Xiu's subordinate officials, and interrogated their private affairs. He first reported Yang Xiu's crimes in detail, and only then spoke to Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，免琇官。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice and dismissed Yang Xiu from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice and dismissed Yang Xiu from office.

sentences.zh: 未-{幾}-，-{復}-使以白衣領職。

translations.literal: Before long, he was again made to hold the post in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he was again made to hold the post in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 琇。

translations.literal: Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiu.

sentences.zh: 景獻皇-{后}-之從父弟也；

translations.literal: He was the empress dowager Jingxian's cousin on the father's side;
translations.idiomatic: He was a cousin of Empress Dowager Jingxian;

sentences.zh: -{後}-將軍王愷，文明皇-{后}-之弟也；

translations.literal: General of the Rear Wang Kai was Empress Dowager Wenming's younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: General of the Rear Wang Kai was Empress Dowager Wenming's younger brother;

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍、侍中石崇，苞之子也。

translations.literal: Shi Chong, Attendant Cavalier and Palace Attendant, was the son of Shi Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chong, Attendant Cavalier and Palace Attendant, was the son of Shi Bao.

sentences.zh: 三人皆富-{於}-財，競以奢侈相髙。

translations.literal: All three were rich in wealth and competed to outdo each other in extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: All three were immensely wealthy and competed to outdo each other in extravagance.

sentences.zh: 愷以□-{台}-澳釜，崇以-{蠟}-代薪；

translations.literal: Wang Kai scrubbed his cauldron with sugar water; Shi Chong used wax for fuel;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai scrubbed his cauldron with sugar water; Shi Chong used wax for fuel;

sentences.zh: 愷作紫絲歩障四十-{里}-，崇作錦歩障五十-{里}-；

translations.literal: Wang Kai made purple silk screens forty li long; Shi Chong made brocade screens fifty li long;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai made purple silk screens forty li long; Shi Chong made brocade screens fifty li long;

sentences.zh: 崇塗屋以椒，愷用赤石脂。

translations.literal: Shi Chong coated his walls with pepper; Wang Kai used red ochre.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chong coated his walls with pepper; Wang Kai used red ochre.

sentences.zh: 帝毎助愷，嘗以珊瑚樹賜之，髙二尺許，愷以示崇，崇便以鐵如意碎之；

translations.literal: The emperor always aided Wang Kai and once bestowed on him a coral tree about two feet high; Wang Kai showed it to Shi Chong, and Shi Chong immediately smashed it with an iron ruyi scepter;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor always favored Wang Kai and once bestowed on him a coral tree about two feet high. Wang Kai showed it to Shi Chong, and Shi Chong immediately smashed it with an iron ruyi scepter;

sentences.zh: 愷怒，以爲疾己之寶。

translations.literal: Wang Kai was angry, thinking Shi Chong envied his treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai was angry, thinking Shi Chong envied his treasure.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「不足多恨，今還卿！」

translations.literal: Shi Chong said, "No need for much regret—I return it to you now!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chong said: "No need for much regret—I return it to you now!"

sentences.zh: 乃命左右悉取其家珊瑚樹，髙三、四尺者六、七株，如愷比者甚衆；

translations.literal: He then ordered his attendants to bring out all the coral trees from his house—six or seven trees three or four feet high, and many like Wang Kai's;
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered his attendants to bring out all the coral trees from his house—six or seven trees three or four feet high, and many like Wang Kai's;

sentences.zh: 愷心光然自失。

translations.literal: Wang Kai's spirit dimmed and he was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai's spirit dimmed and he was utterly defeated.

sentences.zh: 車騎司馬傅-{咸}-上書曰：「先王之治天下，食肉衣帛，皆有其-{制}-。

translations.literal: Fu Xian, Chief Commandant of Cavalry and Chariots, submitted a memorial, saying, "When former kings governed the realm, eating meat and wearing silk each had its proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian, Chief Commandant of Cavalry and Chariots, submitted a memorial: "When former kings governed the realm, eating meat and wearing silk each had its proper measure.

sentences.zh: 竊謂奢侈之費，甚-{於}-天災。

translations.literal: I venture to say that the cost of extravagance exceeds natural disasters.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to say that the cost of extravagance exceeds natural disasters.

sentences.zh: 古者人稠地狹，而有儲蓄，由-{於}-節也。

translations.literal: In antiquity people were dense and land narrow, yet there were reserves—because of frugality.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity people were dense and land narrow, yet there were reserves—because of frugality.

sentences.zh: 今者土曠人稀，而患不足，由-{於}-奢也。

translations.literal: Now land is broad and people sparse, yet there is want—because of extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Now land is broad and people sparse, yet there is want—because of extravagance.

sentences.zh: 欲時人崇儉，當詰其奢。

translations.literal: If one wishes people of the time to honor frugality, one must investigate their extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: If one wishes people to honor frugality, one must investigate their extravagance.

sentences.zh: 奢不見詰，轉相髙尚，無有窮極矣！」

translations.literal: If extravagance is not investigated, it will be passed upward in competition, with no end!"
translations.idiomatic: If extravagance goes uninvestigated, it will be passed upward in competition, with no end!"

sentences.zh: 尚書張華，以文學-{才}-識名重一時，論者皆謂華宜爲三公。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua, Director of the Masters of Writing, was famed throughout his age for literary talent and knowledge; commentators all said Zhang Hua should be one of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua, Director of the Masters of Writing, was famed for literary talent and knowledge; commentators all said he should be one of the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 中書監荀勗、侍中馮紞以伐呉之謀深疾之。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu and Palace Attendant Feng Dan deeply resented him because of the plan to attack Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu and Palace Attendant Feng Dan deeply resented him over the plan to attack Wu.

sentences.zh: 會帝問華：「誰可-{托}--{後}-事者？」

translations.literal: When the emperor asked Zhang Hua, "Who can be entrusted with affairs after me?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked Zhang Hua: "Who can be entrusted with affairs after me?"

sentences.zh: 華對以「明德至親，莫如齊王。」

translations.literal: Zhang Hua answered that "in virtue and closeness, none compares to the Prince of Qi."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua answered: "In virtue and closeness, none compares to the Prince of Qi."

sentences.zh: 由是忤旨，勗因而譖之。

translations.literal: Thereby he went against the emperor's intent, and Xun Xu slandered him on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby he went against the emperor's intent, and Xun Xu slandered him on this account.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以華都督幽州諸軍事。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Zhang Hua was made Area Commander of all military affairs in You Province.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Zhang Hua was made area commander of all military affairs in You Province.

sentences.zh: 華至鎭，撫循夷夏，譽望益振，帝-{復}-欲-{征}-之。

translations.literal: Hua arrived at his post, comforted and guided both barbarians and Chinese, his reputation and prestige increased further, and the emperor again wished to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hua reached his post, he won over both Chinese and non-Chinese subjects, and his reputation grew ever stronger—whereupon the emperor again wished to recall him to court.

sentences.zh: 馮紞侍帝，從容語及-{鐘}-會，紞曰：「會之反，頗由太祖。」

translations.literal: Feng Dan attended the emperor; speaking at ease, they came to Zhong Hui, and Feng said: "Zhong Hui's rebellion owed much to the Founding Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan was attending the emperor when, in relaxed conversation, they came to speak of Zhong Hui. Feng said, "Zhong Hui's rebellion owed much to the Founding Emperor."

sentences.zh: 帝變色曰：「卿是何言邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor changed countenance and said: "What words are these!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened. "What sort of talk is that!"

sentences.zh: 紞免冠謝曰：「臣聞善-{御}-者必知六轡緩急之宜，故孔子以仲由兼人而退之，冉求退弱而進之。

translations.literal: Feng removed his cap and apologized: "I have heard that one who skillfully drives a team must know the proper tension for each of the six reins; hence Confucius dismissed Zhong You for being overbearing, and promoted Ran Qiu for being retiring and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Feng removed his cap and apologized: "I have heard that a skilled charioteer must know how tight or loose to hold each of the six reins. That is why Confucius dismissed Zhong You for being overbearing, and promoted Ran Qiu for being retiring and mild.

sentences.zh: 漢髙祖尊寵五王而夷滅，光武抑損諸將而克終。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han honored and favored the five kings and they were destroyed to the last; Emperor Guangwu restrained and diminished his generals and achieved a peaceful end.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han lavished honors on the five kings, and they were wiped out; Emperor Guangwu kept his generals in check, and his reign ended in peace.

sentences.zh: 非上有仁暴之殊，下有愚智之異也，蓋抑揚與奪使之然耳。

translations.literal: It was not that the rulers above differed in benevolence and brutality or that subjects below differed in folly and wisdom—it was that restraint and elevation, grant and seizure, made things so.
translations.idiomatic: It was not that one ruler was benevolent and another brutal, or that one subject was wise and another foolish. Restraint and promotion, reward and withdrawal—these made the difference.

sentences.zh: -{鐘}-會-{才}-智有限，而太祖誇獎無極，居以重勢，委以大兵，使會自謂算無遺策，功在不賞，遂構凶逆耳。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui's talent and wisdom were limited, yet the Founding Emperor praised and rewarded him without limit, placed him in weighty power, and entrusted him with great armies, so that Hui came to think his plans left nothing out, his achievements beyond reward, and thus he plotted rebellion and treason.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui's talent and wit were limited, yet the Founding Emperor praised and rewarded him without end, gave him great power, and entrusted him with vast armies—until Hui came to believe his plans were flawless and his merit beyond reward, and so he turned to treason.

sentences.zh: 向令太祖録其小能，節以大禮，抑之以威權，納之以軌則，則亂心無由生矣。」

translations.literal: If only the Founding Emperor had counted his small talents, regulated him with great propriety, checked him with authority and power, and bound him to rules and standards, rebellious thoughts would never have arisen."
translations.idiomatic: Had the Founding Emperor instead noted his modest abilities, restrained him with proper ceremony, checked him with authority, and bound him to rule and law, rebellious thoughts would never have taken root."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "True."

sentences.zh: 紞稽首曰：「陛下旣然臣之言，宜思堅冰之漸，勿使如會之徒-{復}-致傾覆。」

translations.literal: Feng prostrated himself and said: "Since Your Majesty assents to my words, you should reflect on the gradual growth of hard ice—do not let men like Zhong Hui again bring ruin."
translations.idiomatic: Feng kowtowed and said, "Since Your Majesty agrees with me, you should remember how solid ice forms by degrees—and not let men like Zhong Hui bring ruin again."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「當今豈-{復}-有如會者邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In the present age, could there again be anyone like Zhong Hui?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "In this age, could there again be anyone like Zhong Hui?"

sentences.zh: 紞因屛左右而言曰：「陛下謀畫之臣，著大功-{於}-天下，-{據}-方鎭、總戎馬者，皆在陛下聖慮矣。」

translations.literal: Feng then dismissed those present and said: "Your Majesty's strategic ministers who have achieved great merit under Heaven, who hold regional commands and command armies—all are within Your Majesty's sacred consideration."
translations.idiomatic: Feng then dismissed those present and said, "Your Majesty's chief strategists—men who have won great merit under Heaven, who hold regional commands and control armies—are all in Your Majesty's mind."

sentences.zh: 帝默然，由是止，不-{征}-華。

translations.literal: The emperor fell silent; on this account he desisted and did not summon Hua.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing. From that point he dropped the matter and did not recall Zhang Hua.

sentences.zh: 三月，安北將軍嚴詢敗慕容渉歸-{於}-昌黎，斬獲萬計。

translations.literal: In the third month, General Who Pacifies the North Yan Xun defeated Murong Shegui at Changli; those killed and captured numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, General Who Pacifies the North Yan Xun defeated Murong Shegui at Changli, killing and capturing tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 魯公賈充老病，上遣皇太子省視起居。

translations.literal: Duke of Lu Jia Chong was aged and ill; the emperor sent the crown prince to visit and inquire after his daily condition.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Lu Jia Chong was old and ill, and the emperor sent the crown prince to visit him and inquire after his health.

sentences.zh: 充自憂諡傳，從子模曰：「是非久自見，不可掩也！」

translations.literal: Jia Chong worried about his posthumous title and biography; his nephew Jia Mo said: "Right and wrong reveal themselves in time—they cannot be concealed!"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong worried about his posthumous name and how history would judge him. His nephew Jia Mo said, "Right and wrong reveal themselves in time—they cannot be hidden forever!"

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚午，充薨。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on gengwu, Jia Chong died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on gengwu, Jia Chong died.

sentences.zh: 世子黎民早卒，無嗣，妻郭槐欲以充外孫韓謐爲世孫，郎中令韓-{咸}-、中尉曹軫諫曰：「禮無異姓爲-{後}-之文，今而行之，是使先公受譏-{於}--{後}-世而懷愧-{於}-地下也。」

translations.literal: The heir Jia Limin died young without offspring; his wife Guo Huai wished to make Jia Chong's grandson by a daughter, Han Mi, heir apparent; Supervisor of the Heir Han Xian and Commandant of the Capital Guards Cao Zhen remonstrated: "The rites provide no precedent for making someone of another surname heir; to do so now would make your late lord suffer ridicule from later ages and shame in the grave."
translations.idiomatic: The heir Jia Limin had died young without issue. His wife Guo Huai wished to make Jia Chong's maternal grandson Han Mi the heir. Supervisor of the Heir Han Xian and Commandant of the Capital Guards Cao Zhen remonstrated: "The rites know no precedent for making a man of another surname one's heir. To do this now would expose your late lord to ridicule in later ages and shame in the grave."

translations.literal: Guo Huai would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai would not listen.

sentences.zh: -{咸}-等上書，救改立嗣，事寢不報。

translations.literal: Han Xian and the others submitted memorials urgently asking that the succession be changed; the matter was shelved without response.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian and the others submitted urgent memorials asking that the succession be changed, but the matter was shelved without reply.

sentences.zh: 槐遂表陳之，-{雲}-充遺意。

translations.literal: Guo Huai thereupon submitted a memorial stating it, saying it was Jia Chong's dying wish.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai then submitted a memorial stating her case, saying it had been Jia Chong's dying wish.

sentences.zh: 帝許之，仍詔「自非功如太宰，始封、無-{後}-者，皆不得以爲比。」

translations.literal: The emperor granted it, and furthermore issued an edict: "Unless one's merit equals the Grand Preceptor and one was enfeoffed at the founding with no heir, none may take this as a precedent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved, and further decreed: "Unless one's merit equals the Grand Preceptor's and one was enfeoffed at the dynasty's founding without an heir, none may cite this as a precedent."

sentences.zh: 及太常議諡，博士秦秀曰：「充悖禮溺情，以亂大倫。

translations.literal: When the Minister of Ceremonies deliberated on the posthumous title, Erudite Qin Xiu said: "Jia Chong violated ritual and drowned in private feeling, disordering the great human bonds.
translations.idiomatic: When the Minister of Ceremonies deliberated on his posthumous title, Erudite Qin Xiu said, "Jia Chong violated ritual and indulged private feeling, overturning the great bonds of human order.

sentences.zh: 昔鄫養外孫莒公子爲-{後}-，《春秋》書『莒人滅鄫』。

translations.literal: In antiquity Zeng raised a grandson of Ju as heir, and the Spring and Autumn Annals records 'The people of Ju destroyed Zeng.'
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Zeng made a grandson of Ju its heir, and the Spring and Autumn Annals records: 'The people of Ju destroyed Zeng.'

sentences.zh: 絶父祖之血食，開朝廷之亂原。

translations.literal: It cut off the blood offerings to fathers and ancestors and opened the source of disorder in the court.
translations.idiomatic: It cut off the sacrificial offerings to fathers and ancestors and opened the wellspring of disorder at court.

sentences.zh: 按《諡法》：『昏亂紀度曰荒』，請諡『荒公』。」

translations.literal: According to the Posthumous Names Canon: 'Confusion of institutions through disorder is called Huang,'—we request the posthumous title 'Duke Huang.'
translations.idiomatic: According to the Posthumous Names Canon, 'One who confuses institutions through disorder is called Huang.' We request the posthumous title Duke Huang."

sentences.zh: 帝不從，更諡曰武。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree and instead gave the posthumous title Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and instead gave him the posthumous title Wu.

sentences.zh: 閏月，丙子，廣陸成侯李胤薨。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on bingzi, Marquis Cheng of Guanglu Li Yin died.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on bingzi, Marquis Cheng of Guanglu Li Yin died.

sentences.zh: 齊王攸德望日隆，荀勗、馮紞、楊珧皆惡之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi's virtue and prestige rose daily; Xun Xu, Feng Dan, and Yang Yao all hated him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi's virtue and prestige rose day by day, and Xun Xu, Feng Dan, and Yang Yao all resented him.

sentences.zh: 紞言-{於}-帝曰：「陛下詔諸侯之國，宜從親者始。

translations.literal: Feng Dan spoke to the emperor: "Your Majesty's edict that princely states should be established—one should begin with the closest kin.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan said to the emperor, "Your Majesty has decreed that the princes should go to their states. One ought to begin with the closest kin.

sentences.zh: 親者莫如齊王，今獨留京師，可乎？」

translations.literal: None is closer than the Prince of Qi, yet he alone remains in the capital—is this acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: No one is closer than the Prince of Qi, yet he alone remains in the capital—is that acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 勗曰：「百僚内外皆歸心齊王，陛下萬歳-{後}-，太子不得立矣。

translations.literal: Xun Xu said: "Officials within and without all look to the Prince of Qi; after Your Majesty's demise, the crown prince will not be able to take the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu said, "Officials inside and outside court all look to the Prince of Qi. After Your Majesty's death, the crown prince will not be able to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 陛下試詔齊王之國，必舉朝以爲不可，則臣言驗矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty may try issuing an edict for the Prince of Qi to go to his state—surely the whole court will deem it unacceptable, and my words will be verified."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty tries ordering the Prince of Qi to his state, the whole court is sure to protest—and then my words will be proved."

sentences.zh: 帝以爲然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought this sound.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，甲申，詔曰：「古者九命作伯，或入毘朝政，或出-{御}-方-{岳}-，其揆一也。

translations.literal: In winter, in the twelfth month, on jiashen, an edict stated: "In antiquity nine investitures made a chief; one might enter to assist court governance or go out to command the regional peaks—the principle was one.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the twelfth month, on jiashen, an edict stated: "In antiquity, nine investitures made a chief minister: one might enter to assist at court, or go out to command the regions—the principle was the same.

sentences.zh: 侍中、司空齊王攸，佐命立勳，劬勞王室，其以爲大司馬、都督靑州諸軍事，侍中如故，仍加崇典禮，主者詳案舊-{制}-施行。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant and Minister of Works Sima You, the Prince of Qi, who assisted in founding the dynasty and established merit, toiling for the royal house—let him be made Grand Marshal and Area Commander of all military affairs in Qing Province, retaining his palace attendant rank, with enhanced ceremonial honors; the responsible offices shall examine the old regulations and implement them.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant and Minister of Works Sima You, the Prince of Qi, who helped establish the dynasty and toiled for the royal house, is appointed Grand Marshal and Area Commander of all military affairs in Qing Province, retaining his rank as Palace Attendant, with enhanced ceremonial honors. The responsible offices shall examine the old regulations and carry them out.

sentences.zh: ?睄以汝南王亮爲太尉、録尚書事、領太子太傅，光祿大夫山濤爲司徒，尚書令衞瓘爲司空。

translations.literal: Then he appointed the Prince of Runan, Sima Liang, Grand Commandant, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; Minister of the Imperial Household Shan Tao as Minister over the Masses; and Director of the Masters of Writing Wei Guan as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Then he appointed the Prince of Runan, Sima Liang, Grand Commandant, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; Shan Tao, Minister of the Imperial Household, as Minister over the Masses; and Wei Guan, Director of the Masters of Writing, as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: -{征}-東大將軍王渾上書，以爲：「攸至親盛德，侔-{於}-周公，宜贊皇朝，與聞政事。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the East Wang Hun submitted a memorial, holding that: "You, being closest in kin and foremost in virtue, equals the Duke of Zhou; you should support the imperial court and take part in governance.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers the East Wang Hun submitted a memorial arguing that the Prince of Qi, being the closest kin and foremost in virtue, was the equal of the Duke of Zhou and ought to support the imperial court and share in governance.

sentences.zh: 今出攸之國，假以都督虚號，而無典戎-{干}-方之實，虧友-{於}-款篤之義，懼非陛下追述先帝、文明太-{后}-待攸之宿意也。

translations.literal: Now, sending You to his state while granting only the empty title of area commander, without real authority over armies and frontiers, violates the brotherly bond of sincere affection—I fear this is not Your Majesty's intent in following the late emperor and Empress Dowager Wenming's longstanding treatment of You.
translations.idiomatic: To send the prince to his state now, giving him only the empty title of area commander without real authority over armies and frontiers, violates the bond of brotherly affection. I fear this is not what Your Majesty intends in honoring the late emperor's and Empress Dowager Wenming's longstanding regard for him.

sentences.zh: 若以同姓寵之太厚，則有呉、楚逆亂之謀，漢之呂、霍、王氏，皆何人也！

translations.literal: If one says kin of the same surname are favored too richly, there were the rebellious schemes of Wu and Chu—yet who were the Lü, Huo, and Wang clans of Han!
translations.idiomatic: If one says that favoring one's own kin too richly invites rebellion like Wu and Chu, then who were the Lü, Huo, and Wang clans of Han?

sentences.zh: -{歴}-觀古今，苟事之輕重所在，不無爲害，唯當任正道而求忠良耳。

translations.literal: Surveying past and present, wherever affairs' weight lies, harm invariably follows; one must only employ the upright Way and seek loyal and good men.
translations.idiomatic: Looking through history, wherever power concentrates, harm follows. One must simply employ the upright Way and seek loyal and worthy men.

sentences.zh: 若以智計猜物，雖親見疑，至-{於}-疎者，庸可保乎！

translations.literal: If one uses cunning schemes to suspect things, even the close come under doubt—how then can the distant be secure!
translations.idiomatic: If one uses cunning to suspect everyone, even the closest kin fall under suspicion—how then can anyone distant be trusted?

sentences.zh: 愚以爲太子太保缺，宜留攸居之，與汝南王亮、楊珧共-{干}-朝事。

translations.literal: I think the Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince's post is vacant—you should retain You in it, sharing court affairs with the Prince of Runan and Yang Yao.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the post of Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince is vacant. The prince should be kept in it, sharing court affairs with the Prince of Runan and Yang Yao.

sentences.zh: 三人齊位，足相持正，旣無偏重相傾之勢，又不失親親仁覆之恩，計之盡善者也。」

translations.literal: The three equal in rank would suffice to check and balance one another—without disproportionate weight to overturn each other, yet without losing the grace of kin loving kin—it would be the most complete plan."
translations.idiomatic: The three, equal in rank, would be enough to check and balance one another—without one side's weight tipping the rest, yet without losing the grace of kinship. It would be the most complete plan.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是扶風王駿、光祿大夫李喜、中護軍羊琇、侍中王濟、甄德皆切諫。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Prince of Fufeng Sima Jun, Minister of the Imperial Household Li Xi, Protector of the Army Yang Xiu, Palace Attendant Wang Ji, and Zhen De all remonstrated urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Prince of Fufeng Sima Jun, Minister of the Imperial Household Li Xi, Protector of the Army Yang Xiu, Palace Attendant Wang Ji, and Zhen De all remonstrated urgently.

sentences.zh: 帝-{並}-不從。

translations.literal: The emperor none of it accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected them all.

sentences.zh: 濟使其妻常山公主及德妻長廣公主倶入，稽顙涕泣，請帝留攸。

translations.literal: Wang Ji had his wife, the Princess of Changshan, and Zhen De's wife, the Princess of Chaguang, both enter together; they kowtowed, weeping, and begged the emperor to retain You.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji sent in his wife, the Princess of Changshan, and Zhen De's wife, the Princess of Chaguang. Both kowtowed, weeping, and begged the emperor to keep the Prince of Qi at court.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謂侍中王戎曰：「兄弟至親，今出齊王，自是朕家事，而甄德、王濟連遣婦來生哭人邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and said to Palace Attendant Wang Rong: "Brothers are closest kin—sending the Prince of Qi out now is my family affair—yet Zhen De and Wang Ji keep sending their wives to come weep and wail at me!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and said to Palace Attendant Wang Rong, "Brothers are the closest of kin. Sending the Prince of Qi away is my family affair—yet Zhen De and Wang Ji keep sending their wives to come mourn and wail before me!"

sentences.zh: 乃出濟爲國子祭酒，德爲大鴻臚。

translations.literal: He then transferred Wang Ji to Director of the National University and Zhen De to Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: He then transferred Wang Ji to Director of the National University and Zhen De to Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 羊琇與北軍中候成粲謀見楊珧，手刃殺之；

translations.literal: Yang Xiu and Central Army Commandant Cheng Can plotted to visit Yang Yao and kill him with their own blades;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiu and Central Army Commandant Cheng Can plotted to visit Yang Yao and kill him with their own hands;

sentences.zh: 珧知之，辭疾不出，諷有司奏琇，左遷太-{僕}-。

translations.literal: Yao learned of it, pleaded illness and did not go out, and hinted that the authorities memorialize against Xiu, who was demoted to Grand Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: Yao learned of it, pleaded illness, and stayed away; he hinted that the authorities should memorialize against Xiu, who was demoted to Grand Coachman.

sentences.zh: 琇憤怨，-{發}-病卒。

translations.literal: Xiu, resentful and bitter, fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu, full of resentment, fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 李喜亦以年老遜位，卒-{於}-家。

translations.literal: Li Xi also yielded his office on account of age and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi also yielded his office on account of age and died at home.

sentences.zh: 喜在朝，姻親故人，與之分衣共食，而未嘗私以王官，人以此稱之。

translations.literal: While Li Xi was at court, he shared clothes and food with kinsmen and old friends, yet never privately granted them princely offices—people praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Xi served at court, he shared clothes and food with kinsmen and old friends, yet never privately gave them princely offices—and people praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 是歳，散騎常侍薛瑩卒。

translations.literal: That year, Regular Attendant of Cavalry Xue Ying died.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Regular Attendant of Cavalry Xue Ying died.

sentences.zh: 或謂呉郡陸喜曰：「瑩-{於}-呉士當爲第一乎？」

translations.literal: Someone said to Lu Xi of Wu Commandery: "Among men of Wu, should Ying rank first?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Lu Xi of Wu Commandery, "Among Wu scholars, should Xue Ying rank first?"

sentences.zh: 喜曰：「瑩在四五之間，安得爲第一！

translations.literal: Lu Xi said: "Ying falls between fourth and fifth—how can he be first!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xi said, "Ying falls between fourth and fifth—how can he be first!

sentences.zh: 夫以孫皓無道，呉國之士，沈默其體，潛而勿用者，第一也；

translations.literal: Considering Sun Hao's lack of the Way, among Wu scholars: those who kept their bodies silent and withdrew without serving rank first;
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Hao's wicked rule, among Wu scholars those who kept silent, withdrew, and refused to serve ranked first;

sentences.zh: 避尊居卑，祿以代耕者，第二也；

translations.literal: those who avoided high rank and accepted low, taking salary as a farmer's substitute rank second;
translations.idiomatic: those who shunned high rank for low office and took salary as a farmer's substitute ranked second;

sentences.zh: 侃然體國，執正不懼者，第三也；

translations.literal: those who stood upright for the state and held to rectitude without fear rank third;
translations.idiomatic: those who stood upright for the state and held to principle without fear ranked third;

sentences.zh: 斟酌時宜，時獻微益者，第四也；

translations.literal: those who weighed the times and occasionally offered small benefit rank fourth;
translations.idiomatic: those who weighed the times and occasionally offered modest counsel ranked fourth;

sentences.zh: 温恭修愼，不爲謅首者」第五也；

translations.literal: those who were warm, respectful, cautious, and careful, who did not serve as chief flatterer rank fifth;"
translations.idiomatic: those who were warm, respectful, and careful, and did not play the chief flatterer ranked fifth;"

sentences.zh: 過此以往，不足-{複}-數。

translations.literal: Beyond these, they are not worth counting.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these, they are not worth counting.

sentences.zh: 故彼上士多淪沒而遠悔吝，中士有聲位而近禍殃。

translations.literal: Thus those highest scholars mostly sank into obscurity with distant regret, while middling scholars gained fame and position but drew near calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the highest scholars mostly sank into obscurity with distant regret, while middling scholars won fame and office but drew near disaster.

sentences.zh: 觀瑩之處身本末，又安得爲第一乎！」

translations.literal: Considering how Ying conducted himself from beginning to end—how can he be first!"
translations.idiomatic: Looking at how Ying conducted himself from start to finish—how can he be first!"

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲申，以尚書右-{僕}-射魏舒爲左-{僕}-射，下邳王晃爲右-{僕}-射。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on jiashen, Right Deputy Director of the Masters of Writing Wei Shu was made Left Deputy Director, and the Prince of Xiapi Sima Huang was made Right Deputy Director.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on jiashen, Right Deputy Director of the Masters of Writing Wei Shu was made Left Deputy Director, and the Prince of Xiapi Sima Huang was made Right Deputy Director.

sentences.zh: 晃，孚之子也。

translations.literal: Huang was the son of Sima Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was the son of Sima Fu.

sentences.zh: 戊午，新沓康伯山濤薨。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the newly ennobled Duke Kang of Xinta, Shan Tao, died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Duke Kang of Xinta, Shan Tao, died.

sentences.zh: 帝命太常議崇錫齊王之物。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Minister of Ceremonies to deliberate on the elevated gifts for the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Minister of Ceremonies to deliberate on the honors to be granted the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 博士庾敷、太叔廣、劉暾、繆蔚、郭頤、秦秀、傅珍上表曰：「昔周選建德以左右王室，周公、康叔、聃季，皆入爲三公，明股肱之任重，守地之位輕也。

translations.literal: Erudites Yu Fu, Taishu Guang, Liu Tun, Miao Wei, Guo Yi, Qin Xiu, and Fu Zhen submitted a memorial stating: "In antiquity Zhou selected those who established virtue to support the royal house on left and right; the Duke of Zhou, Uncle Kang, and Uncle Dan all entered court as the Three Dukes, making clear that the burden of the arms and thighs was weighty and the position of guarding territory was light.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites Yu Fu, Taishu Guang, Liu Tun, Miao Wei, Guo Yi, Qin Xiu, and Fu Zhen submitted a memorial: "In antiquity Zhou chose men of established virtue to support the royal house. The Duke of Zhou, Uncle Kang, and Uncle Dan all entered court as the Three Dukes, showing that the burden of serving as the king's arms and thighs was weighty, while guarding a domain was comparatively light.

sentences.zh: 漢諸王侯，位在丞相、三公上，其入贊朝政者，乃有兼宮，其出之國，亦不-{復}-假-{台}-司虚名爲隆寵也。

translations.literal: Han princes and marquises ranked above the chancellor and the Three Dukes; those who entered to assist court governance might hold concurrent offices, but when they went out to their states they were not again given empty titles of the Three Platforms as inflated favor.
translations.idiomatic: Han princes and marquises outranked the chancellor and the Three Dukes. Those who entered to assist at court might hold concurrent offices, but when they went out to their states they were not given empty titles of the Three Platforms merely as inflated favor.

sentences.zh: 今使齊王賢邪，則不宜以母弟之親尊居魯、衞之常職；

translations.literal: If the Prince of Qi is worthy now, then it is not fitting to honor a younger brother by the mother's line with the ordinary duties of Lu and Wei;
translations.idiomatic: If the Prince of Qi is worthy, it is not fitting to honor a younger brother of the same mother with the ordinary duties of Lu and Wei;

sentences.zh: 不賢邪，不宜大啓土宇，表建東海也。

translations.literal: If he is not worthy, it is not fitting to greatly open territory and proclaim the establishment of a realm like the Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: If he is not worthy, it is not fitting to grant him vast territory and proclaim a great eastern domain.

sentences.zh: 古禮，三公無職，坐而論道，不聞以方任嬰之。

translations.literal: In ancient ritual the Three Dukes had no fixed duties; they sat and discussed the Way—it is not heard that they were burdened with regional responsibilities.
translations.idiomatic: By ancient ritual the Three Dukes had no fixed duties; they sat and discussed the Way. One never hears of them being burdened with regional command.

sentences.zh: 惟宣王救急朝夕，然-{後}-命召穆公-{征}-淮夷，故其詩曰：『徐方不回，王曰旋歸。』

translations.literal: Only when King Xuan of Zhou was in urgent peril day and night did he then command Duke Mu of Shao to campaign against the Huaiyi; hence the ode says: 'Xu had not yet submitted when the king said, Turn back and return.'
translations.idiomatic: Only when King Xuan faced urgent peril day and night did he command Duke Mu of Shao to campaign against the Huaiyi. Hence the ode says: 'Xu had not yet submitted when the king said, Turn back and return.'

sentences.zh: 宰相不得久在外也。

translations.literal: A chief minister must not long remain abroad.
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister must not long remain abroad.

sentences.zh: 今天下已定，六合爲家，將數延三事，與論太平之基，而更出之，去王城二千-{里}-，違舊章矣。』

translations.literal: Now the realm is settled and the six directions are one household; you will repeatedly summon the Three Excellencies to discuss the foundation of peace—yet you send him out again, two thousand li from the royal capital, violating the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is settled and all under Heaven is one household. You will repeatedly summon the Three Excellencies to discuss the foundations of peace—yet you send him out again, two thousand li from the capital, in violation of ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 敷，純之子；

translations.literal: Fu was the son of Chun;
translations.idiomatic: Fu was the son of Chun;

sentences.zh: 暾，毅之子也。

translations.literal: Tun was the son of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Tun was the son of Yi.

sentences.zh: 敷旣具草，先以呈純，純不禁。

translations.literal: After Fu had completed the draft, he first presented it to Chun; Chun did not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu had completed the draft, he first showed it to Chun, who did not forbid it.

sentences.zh: 事過太常鄭默、博士祭酒曹-{志}-，-{志}-愴然歎曰：「安有如此之-{才}-，如此之親，不得樹本助化，而遠出海隅！

translations.literal: The matter passed before Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Mo and Erudite Libationer Cao Zhi; Zhi sighed in grief and said: "How can there be talent such as this, kinship such as this, yet he cannot plant his roots and assist in transformation, but is sent far to the edge of the sea!
translations.idiomatic: The matter passed before Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Mo and Erudite Libationer Cao Zhi. Zhi sighed in grief and said, "How can there be talent such as this, kinship such as this—and yet he cannot take root and help govern, but is sent far to the edge of the sea!

sentences.zh: 晉室之隆，其殆矣乎！」

translations.literal: The glory of the house of Jin—is it not in peril!"
translations.idiomatic: The glory of the house of Jin—is it not in peril!"

sentences.zh: 乃奏議曰：「古之夾輔王室，同姓則周公、異姓則太公，皆身居朝廷，五世反葬。

translations.literal: He then submitted a deliberation stating: "Those who flanked and supported the royal house in antiquity—of the same surname there was the Duke of Zhou, of another surname there was Grand Duke Wang—all personally dwelt at court, and for five generations were buried back home.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a deliberation: "Those who supported the royal house in antiquity—of the same surname there was the Duke of Zhou, of another surname there was Grand Duke Wang—all personally served at court, and for five generations were buried back home.

sentences.zh: 及其衰也，雖有五霸代興，豈與周、召之治同日而論哉！

translations.literal: When Zhou declined, though the Five Hegemons rose in succession, how could that be discussed on the same day as the governance of Zhou and Shao!
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou declined, though the Five Hegemons rose in turn, how could that be spoken of in the same breath as the governance of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao!

sentences.zh: 自羲皇以來，豈一姓所能獨有！

translations.literal: From the time of Fu Xi and the Yellow Emperor onward, how could one surname alone possess all!
translations.idiomatic: From Fu Xi and the Yellow Emperor onward, how could one surname alone possess the realm forever!

sentences.zh: 當推至公之心，與天下共其利害，乃能享國久長。

translations.literal: One must extend the utmost public-minded heart and share benefit and harm with all under Heaven—only then can one enjoy the state long.
translations.idiomatic: One must extend the utmost public-minded heart and share benefit and harm with all under Heaven—only then can one enjoy the state long.

sentences.zh: 是以秦、魏欲獨擅其權而-{才}-得沒身，周、漢能分其利而親疎爲用，此前事之明驗也。

translations.literal: Thus Qin and Wei wished to monopolize power alone and obtained only death in body; Zhou and Han were able to divide benefit and employ both close and distant kin—this is the clear proof of earlier events.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Qin and Wei sought to monopolize power and gained only death in their own day; Zhou and Han were able to share benefit and employ both close and distant kin—this is the clear lesson of history.

sentences.zh: -{志}-以爲當如博士等議。」

translations.literal: Zhi held that one should follow the deliberation of the erudites and the others."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi held that the court should follow the erudites' deliberation."

sentences.zh: 帝覽之，大怒曰：「曹-{志}-尚不明吾心，況四海乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor read it and grew greatly angry, saying: "Cao Zhi still does not understand my heart—how much less all under Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and flew into a rage. "If Cao Zhi still does not understand my heart, how much less all under Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 且謂：「博士不答所問而答所不問，橫造異論。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The erudites did not answer what was asked but answered what was not asked, recklessly fabricating divergent opinions."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The erudites did not answer what was asked but answered what was not asked, recklessly inventing contrary opinions."

sentences.zh: 下有司策免鄭默。

translations.literal: He ordered the responsible offices to dismiss Zheng Mo by edict.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the responsible offices to dismiss Zheng Mo by edict.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是尚書朱整、褚等奏：「-{志}-等侵官離局，迷惘朝廷，崇飾晉言，假-{托}-無諱，請收-{志}-等付廷尉科罪。」

translations.literal: Thereupon Directors of the Masters of Writing Zhu Zheng, Chu, and others memorialized: "Zhi and the others overstepped their offices and departed from their duties, bewildering the court, exalting and embellishing Jin rhetoric, falsely relying on frank speech without reserve—we request that Zhi and the others be taken and handed to the Minister of Justice for punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Directors of the Masters of Writing Zhu Zheng, Chu, and others memorialized: "Zhi and the others overstepped their offices, departed from their duties, and misled the court, exalting Jin rhetoric under the pretense of frank speech. We request that Zhi and the others be arrested and handed to the Minister of Justice for punishment."

sentences.zh: 詔免-{志}-官，以公還第；

translations.literal: An edict dismissed Zhi from office and sent him home with ducal rank;
translations.idiomatic: An edict dismissed Zhi from office and sent him home with ducal rank;

sentences.zh: 其-{餘}-皆付廷尉科罪。

translations.literal: the rest were all handed to the Minister of Justice for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: the rest were all handed to the Minister of Justice for punishment.

sentences.zh: 庾純詣廷尉自首：「敷以議草見示，愚淺-{聽}-之。」

translations.literal: Yu Chun went to the Minister of Justice and confessed: "Fu showed me the draft deliberation, and in my folly I assented to it."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun went to the Minister of Justice and confessed: "Fu showed me the draft deliberation, and in my folly I assented to it."

sentences.zh: 詔免純罪。

translations.literal: An edict exempted Chun from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict exempted Chun from punishment.

sentences.zh: 廷尉劉頌奏敷等大不敬，當棄市。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Liu Song memorialized that Fu and the others had committed great disrespect and should be executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Liu Song memorialized that Fu and the others had committed great disrespect and should be executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 尚書奏請報-{聽}-廷尉行刑。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing memorialized requesting approval for the Minister of Justice to carry out the execution.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing memorialized requesting approval for the Minister of Justice to carry out the execution.

sentences.zh: 尚書夏侯駿曰：「官立八座，正爲此時。」

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Xiahou Jun said: "The Eight Seats were established precisely for moments such as this."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Xiahou Jun said, "The Eight Seats were established precisely for moments such as this."

sentences.zh: 乃獨爲駁議。

translations.literal: He then alone submitted a dissenting memorial.
translations.idiomatic: With that, he alone submitted a dissenting memorial.

sentences.zh: 左-{僕}-射下邳王晃亦從駿議。

translations.literal: The Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Sima Huang, Prince of Xiapi, also followed Jun's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Sima Huang, Prince of Xiapi, sided with Jun's proposal as well.

sentences.zh: 奏留中七日，乃詔曰：「敷是議主，應爲戮首；

translations.literal: The memorial was kept in the palace for seven days, after which an edict stated: "Fu is the chief proponent of this proposal and ought to be executed as the ringleader;
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was held at court for seven days before an edict was issued: "Fu is the chief advocate of this proposal and should pay with his life as the ringleader;

sentences.zh: 但敷家人自首，宜-{並}-廣等七人皆丐其死命，-{並}-除名。」

translations.literal: But because Fu's family surrendered themselves, Yi Bingguang and the other six men all begged that his life be spared, and all seven were removed from office."
translations.idiomatic: But since Fu's family had come forward to confess, Yi Bingguang and the six others all pleaded for his life, and all seven were stripped of their posts."

sentences.zh: 二月，詔以濟南郡益齊國。

translations.literal: In the second month, an edict ordered that Jinan commandery be added to augment the Kingdom of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, an edict transferred Jinan commandery to enlarge the Kingdom of Qi.

sentences.zh: 己-{丑}-，立齊王攸子長樂亭侯寔爲北海王，命攸備物典策，設軒轅之樂，六佾之舞，黃鉞朝車，乘輿之副從焉。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, Chang Le District Marquis Shi, son of the Prince of Qi, You, was established as Prince of Beihai; the emperor ordered You to prepare the ceremonial regalia and patent of investiture, set out the Xuanyuan music, the dance of six rows, the yellow battle-axe and court carriage, with the secondary imperial carriage accompanying.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jichou, Chang Le District Marquis Shi, son of Prince of Qi Sima You, was invested as Prince of Beihai. You was commanded to furnish the ceremonial patent and regalia—the Xuanyuan music, the six-row dance, the yellow battle-axe and court carriage, with a secondary imperial carriage in attendance.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛-{丑}-朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day of the cycle (xinchou), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the new moon of the day xinchou, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 齊獻王攸憤怨-{發}-病，乞守先-{後}-陵。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Qi, You, grew ill from resentment and indignation, and requested to guard the tombs of the former emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Qi, Sima You, fell ill with resentment and grief, and petitioned to serve as guardian of the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，遣-{御}-醫診視。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit this and sent imperial physicians to examine and treat him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and dispatched court physicians to examine him.

sentences.zh: 諸醫希旨，皆言無疾。

translations.literal: The physicians, seeking to please the emperor's wishes, all declared he had no illness.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the emperor's wishes, the physicians all declared him healthy.

sentences.zh: 河南尹向雄諫曰：「陛下子弟雖多，然有德望者少；

translations.literal: The Intendant of Henan, Xiang Xiong, remonstrated, saying: "Although Your Majesty's sons and younger brothers are many, yet those with virtue and reputation are few;
translations.idiomatic: The Intendant of Henan, Xiang Xiong, remonstrated: "Your Majesty has many sons and brothers, but few of them enjoy real moral authority;

sentences.zh: 齊王臣居京邑，所益實深，不可不思也。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi, Your Majesty's subject, dwells in the capital; the benefit he brings is truly great—this cannot fail to be given thought."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Sima You, your own kinsman, remains in the capital—the good he does the realm is profound, and Your Majesty must not take that lightly.

sentences.zh: 帝不納，雄憤恚而卒。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept this. Xiong died in indignation and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored the counsel. Xiong died consumed by anger and grief.

sentences.zh: 攸疾轉篤，帝猶催上道。

translations.literal: You's illness grew increasingly severe, yet the emperor still pressed him to set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: As You's illness worsened, the emperor still pressed him to depart for his post.

sentences.zh: 攸自強入辭，素持容儀，疾雖困，尚自整厲，舉止如常，帝益疑其無疾；

translations.literal: You forced himself to enter and take leave. He had always maintained proper bearing; though his illness was severe, he still composed himself, and his conduct was as usual. The emperor came to suspect all the more that he had no illness.
translations.idiomatic: You rallied his strength to come in and bid farewell. Always punctilious in bearing, though gravely ill he still held himself upright and behaved as if nothing were wrong. The emperor only grew more convinced he was feigning sickness.

sentences.zh: 辭出數日，嘔血而薨。

translations.literal: Several days after taking his leave and departing, he vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: A few days after his farewell, he vomited blood and died.

sentences.zh: 帝往臨喪，攸子冏號踴，訴父病爲醫所誣。

translations.literal: The emperor went in person to attend the mourning. You's son Gong wailed and leaped in grief, declaring that his father's illness had been misrepresented by the physicians.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person to pay respects at the bier. You's son Sima Jiong wailed and beat his breast, accusing the physicians of having lied about his father's condition.

sentences.zh: 詔卽誅醫，以冏爲嗣。

translations.literal: An edict immediately ordered the physicians executed and made Gong his successor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once ordered the physicians put to death and named Jiong his heir.

sentences.zh: 初，帝愛攸甚篤，爲荀勗、馮紞等所構，欲爲身-{後}-之慮，故出之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had loved You very deeply. He was slandered by Xun Xu, Feng Dan, and others. For the sake of considerations about their own futures, they therefore had him sent away.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor had loved You with exceptional devotion. Xun Xu, Feng Dan, and their faction slandered him and, looking out for their own prospects after his death, engineered his removal from court.

sentences.zh: 及薨，帝哀慟不已。

translations.literal: When he died, the emperor's grief and sorrow would not cease.
translations.idiomatic: When You died, the emperor could not stop grieving.

sentences.zh: 馮紞侍側，曰：「齊王名過其實，天下歸之，今自薨殞，社稷之福也，陛下何哀之過！」

translations.literal: Feng Dan, attending at his side, said: "The Prince of Qi's reputation exceeded his substance, and all under Heaven looked to him. Now that he has died of himself, this is fortune for the altars of state—why does Your Majesty mourn so excessively!"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan, standing at his side, said, "The Prince of Qi's fame outran his merit, and the realm looked to him with hope. Now that he has died a natural death, the altars of state are the better for it. Why grieve so deeply, Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 帝收涙而止。

translations.literal: The emperor wiped away his tears and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor checked his tears and fell silent.

sentences.zh: 詔攸喪禮依安平獻王故事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that You's funeral rites follow the precedent of Prince Xian of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed that You's funeral follow the precedent set for Prince Xian of Anping.

sentences.zh: 攸舉動以禮，鮮有過事，雖帝亦敬憚之。

translations.literal: You's conduct was governed by ritual, and he seldom had any transgression. Even the emperor respected and stood in awe of him.
translations.idiomatic: You conducted himself scrupulously by the rites and rarely erred. Even the emperor treated him with respect mingled with caution.

sentences.zh: 毎引之同處，必擇言而-{後}--{發}-。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor drew him into his company, You always chose his words before speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor kept him close, You was always careful to choose his words before he spoke.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，己亥，琅邪武王伷薨。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on the day jihai, Prince Wu of Langya, Zhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on the day jihai, Prince Wu of Langya, Sima Zhou, died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，以尚書左-{僕}-射魏舒爲司徒。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Wei Shu, was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, Wei Shu, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 河南及荊、揚等六州大水。

translations.literal: Henan and Jing, Yang, and four other provinces suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: Massive flooding struck six provinces, including Henan, Jing, and Yang.

sentences.zh: 歸命侯孫皓卒。

translations.literal: Marquis Guiming, Sun Hao, died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao, the Marquis of Guiming, died.

sentences.zh: 是歳，鮮卑慕容渉歸卒。

translations.literal: In this year, Murong Shegui of the Xianbei died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Murong Shegui of the Xianbei died.

sentences.zh: 弟刪篡立，將殺渉歸子廆，廆亡匿-{於}-遼東徐郁家。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shan usurped the leadership. About to kill Shegui's son Hui, he fled and hid in the home of Xu Yu in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shan seized power in a coup. When Shan moved to kill Shegui's son Murong Hui, Hui fled into hiding with Xu Yu of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己亥，有靑龍二，見武庫井中。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day jihai, two azure dragons were seen in the well of the armory.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day jihai, two azure dragons appeared in the well of the imperial armory.

sentences.zh: 帝觀之，有喜色。

translations.literal: The emperor went to look at them and showed a delighted expression.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to view them and could not hide his pleasure.

sentences.zh: 百官將賀，尚書左-{僕}-射劉毅表曰：「昔龍降夏庭，卒爲周禍。

translations.literal: The officials were about to offer congratulations when the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Liu Yi, submitted a memorial saying: "In the past a dragon descended in the Xia court, and in the end it became calamity for Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: As the officials prepared to offer congratulations, the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Liu Yi, submitted a memorial: "In antiquity a dragon appeared in the Xia court, yet in the end it brought disaster upon Zhou.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱『潛龍勿用，陽在下也。』

translations.literal: The Book of Changes states: "The hidden dragon—do not employ it; the yang is below."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "The hidden dragon must not be deployed—the yang force still lies below."

sentences.zh: 尋案舊典，無賀龍之禮。」

translations.literal: Upon searching the old precedents, there is no rite for congratulating the appearance of a dragon."
translations.idiomatic: A search of the ancient records finds no ceremony for celebrating the appearance of a dragon."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 初，陳群以吏部不能審核天下之士，故令郡國各置中正，州置大中正，皆取本士之人任朝廷官，德充-{才}-盛者爲之，使銓次等級以爲九品，有言行修著則升之，道義虧缺則降之，吏部憑之以補授百官。

translations.literal: Initially, because Chen Qun considered that the Ministry of Personnel could not examine all the men under Heaven, he ordered each commandery and state to appoint a Rectifier, and each province to appoint a Grand Rectifier. All were to be natives of the locality who held office at court, men of abundant virtue and talent. They were to rank grades in order as the nine ranks; those whose conduct and speech were outstanding were promoted, those deficient in moral principle were demoted, and the Ministry of Personnel relied on this to appoint all officials.
translations.idiomatic: At first Chen Qun, finding that the Ministry of Personnel could not vet talent across the realm, ordered every commandery and state to appoint a Rectifier and every province a Grand Rectifier. These posts went to local men serving at court who possessed both virtue and ability. They were to rank candidates into nine grades—promoting those of proven conduct and demoting those who fell short in moral principle—while the Ministry of Personnel used their ratings to fill all offices.

sentences.zh: 行之浸久，中正或非其人，-{奸}-敝日滋。

translations.literal: As the system was practiced over time, the Rectifiers were not always the right men, and corruption and abuse increased daily.
translations.idiomatic: As the system endured, the Rectifiers were not always worthy appointees, and corruption grew worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 劉毅上疎曰：「今立中正，定九品，髙下任意，榮辱在手，操人主之威福，奪天朝之權威，公無考校之負，私無告訐之忌，用心百態，營求萬端，廉讓之風滅，爭訟之俗成，臣竊爲聖朝恥之！

translations.literal: Liu Yi submitted a memorial saying: "Now that Rectifiers are established and the nine ranks fixed, high and low are decided at will and honor and shame rest in their hands. They wield the sovereign's favor and punishment, usurp the imperial court's authority, bear no public burden of examination, and have no private fear of denunciation. Their minds take a hundred forms and their scheming follows ten thousand paths. The spirit of modesty and yielding is extinguished, and the custom of litigation is established. Your servant is privately ashamed for the holy dynasty!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi submitted a memorial: "With Rectifiers in place and the nine ranks fixed, they decide rank at whim and hold honor and disgrace in their hands. They wield the sovereign's rewards and punishments and seize authority that belongs to the throne. They bear no public duty of verification and fear no private accusation. Their minds twist through every guise and their scheming knows no limit. The spirit of modest yielding is dead, and a culture of litigation thrives. Your servant is ashamed for this sacred dynasty!

sentences.zh: 蓋中正之設，-{於}-損政之道有八；

translations.literal: In all, the establishment of Rectifiers has eight ways in which it harms governance;
translations.idiomatic: Taken together, the Rectifier system inflicts eight distinct harms upon good government:

sentences.zh: 髙下逐強弱，是非隨興衰，一人之身，旬日異狀，上品無寒門，下品無勢族，一也。

translations.literal: Rank follows strength and weakness, right and wrong follow rise and decline; one man's standing changes within ten days; there are no humble families in the upper ranks and no powerful clans in the lower ranks—the first.
translations.idiomatic: Rank follows power, not merit; judgment shifts with a family's fortunes; a single man's rating can change within ten days; no humble house reaches the top grade, and no great clan sinks to the bottom—the first harm.

sentences.zh: 置州都者，本取州裡淸議-{咸}-所歸服，將以鎭異同，一言議也。

translations.literal: The provincial commissioners were originally chosen from those whom the pure critics of the province all deferred to, so as to suppress disagreement and settle matters with one voice.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial commissioners were meant to be men whom local opinion universally respected, to settle disputes and speak with one voice—the second intended purpose, now perverted.

sentences.zh: 今重其任而輕其人，使駁違之論橫-{於}-州裡，嫌仇之隙結-{於}-大臣，二也。

translations.literal: Now their responsibilities are heavy but the men appointed are unworthy, so contradictory opinions spread across the provinces and enmities among great ministers are cemented—the second.
translations.idiomatic: Today the office carries great weight but unworthy men fill it, so contradictory verdicts spread through every province and feuds among senior ministers deepen—the second harm.

sentences.zh: 本立格之體，爲九品者，謂-{才}-德有優劣，倫輩有首尾也。

translations.literal: The original framework of the nine ranks was meant to distinguish superior and inferior talent and virtue, and to set the head and tail among peers of the same generation.
translations.idiomatic: The nine-rank framework was meant to distinguish better from worse in talent and virtue, and to order peers from first to last within each grade.

sentences.zh: 今乃使優劣易地，首尾倒錯，三也。

translations.literal: Now the superior and inferior change places and head and tail are reversed—the third.
translations.idiomatic: Now the worthy and unworthy trade places and the proper order is turned upside down—the third harm.

sentences.zh: 陛下賞善罰惡，無不裁之以法，獨置中正，委以一國之重，曾無賞罰之防，又禁人不得訴訟，使之縱橫任意，無所顧憚，諸受枉者，抱怨積直，不獲上聞，四也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty rewards good and punishes evil, all governed by law; yet Rectifiers alone are entrusted with a state's weight of authority without any check of reward or punishment, and people are forbidden to bring suit, so that they act at will without restraint. Those who suffer injustice accumulate grievances and cannot make them heard at court—the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rewards virtue and punishes wrongdoing under the law in every other matter, yet Rectifiers alone are entrusted with a province's worth of power without any check, and the wronged are forbidden to sue. They act without restraint, while those who suffer injustice pile up grievances that never reach the throne—the fourth harm.

sentences.zh: 一國之士，多者千數，或流徙異邦，或取給殊方，-{面}-猶不識，況盡其-{才}-！

translations.literal: The men of a single state number in the thousands; some have been displaced to other lands, some live and earn their keep in distant places—their faces are not even known, how much less their full talent!
translations.idiomatic: The men of a single state number in the thousands; some have been displaced abroad, others live and work far from home—the Rectifier does not even know their faces, let alone their full abilities!

sentences.zh: 而中正知與不知，皆當品狀，采譽-{於}--{台}-府，納毀-{於}-流言，任己則有不識之蔽，-{聽}-受則有彼此之偏，五也。

translations.literal: Yet whether Rectifiers know a man or not, they must all issue evaluations; they gather praise from the offices and accept slander from rumor. If they rely on themselves, they suffer the blindness of ignorance; if they listen to others, they suffer the bias of partiality—the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whether they know a candidate or not, Rectifiers must still issue formal ratings—gathering praise from the bureaucracy and accepting slander from gossip. Trust themselves and they are blind; trust others and they are partial—the fifth harm.

sentences.zh: 凡求人-{才}-者，欲以治民也，今當官著效者或附卑品，在官無績者更獲髙敘，是爲抑功實而隆空名，長浮華而廢考績，六也。

translations.literal: In seeking talent, the aim is to govern the people. Yet now those who achieve results in office are sometimes given low ranks, while those who achieve nothing in office receive higher appointments. This suppresses real merit and elevates empty reputation, nourishes showiness and abandons performance review—the sixth.
translations.idiomatic: Talent is sought to govern the people, yet officials who produce results are sometimes ranked low while those who achieve nothing win higher appointments. Real merit is suppressed and empty reputation exalted; showiness flourishes while performance review withers—the sixth harm.

sentences.zh: 凡官不同人，事不同能。

translations.literal: Every office suits a different man, and every task requires a different ability.
translations.idiomatic: Every office suits a different man, and every task demands a different skill.

sentences.zh: 今不狀其-{才}-之所宜而但第爲九品，以品取人，或非-{才}-能之所長，以狀取人，則爲本品之所限，徒結白論而品狀相妨，七也。

translations.literal: Now, without describing what each man's talent suits, they simply assign one of nine ranks. If men are chosen by rank, they may not possess the ability required; if chosen by the written evaluation, they are constrained by that rank's limits. Empty disputes multiply while rank and evaluation contradict each other—the seventh.
translations.idiomatic: Today no account is taken of what each man's talents suit; men are simply slotted into one of nine grades. Appoint by grade and you may miss the man's true strength; appoint by evaluation and you are trapped within that grade's limits. Empty argument flourishes while rank and merit pull against each other—the seventh harm.

sentences.zh: 九品所下不彰其罪，所上不列其善，各任愛憎，以植其私，天下之人焉得不懈德行而鋭人事，八也。

translations.literal: When the nine ranks demote, they do not expose the man's faults; when they promote, they do not list his virtues. Each follows private affection to serve private ends. How can men under Heaven fail to neglect virtue and pursue worldly maneuvering—the eighth.
translations.idiomatic: Demotions under the nine-rank system do not spell out a man's faults; promotions do not record his virtues. Each Rectifier follows private liking to serve private ends. How can men under Heaven not neglect moral cultivation and sharpen their appetite for intrigue—the eighth harm.

sentences.zh: 由此論之，職名中正，實爲-{奸}-府；

translations.literal: Judging from this, an office called Rectifier is in truth a nest of corruption;
translations.idiomatic: On these grounds, an office called Rectifier is in truth a nest of corruption;

sentences.zh: 事名九品，而有八損。

translations.literal: a system called the nine ranks, yet bearing eight harms.
translations.idiomatic: a system called the nine ranks, yet bearing eight harms.

sentences.zh: 古今之失，莫大-{於}-此！

translations.literal: Among the errors of past and present, none is greater than this!
translations.idiomatic: Among the failures of past and present governance, none is greater than this!

sentences.zh: 愚臣以爲宜罷中正，除九品，棄魏氏之敝法，更立一代之美-{制}-。」

translations.literal: Your foolish servant believes that Rectifiers should be abolished, the nine ranks eliminated, Wei's defective law discarded, and a fine institution for a new age established."
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant believes the Rectifiers should be abolished, the nine ranks eliminated, Wei's broken law cast aside, and a worthy institution for a new age established in its place."

sentences.zh: 太尉汝南王亮、司空衞瓘亦上疎曰：「魏氏承喪亂之-{後}-，人士流移，考詳無地，故立九品之-{制}-，粗且爲一時選用之本耳。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant, Sima Liang, Prince of Runan, and the Minister of Works, Wei Guan, also submitted a memorial saying: "Wei inherited the aftermath of chaos and ruin; scholars were displaced and there was no ground on which to examine them thoroughly. Therefore the nine-rank system was established, roughly serving for the time being as a basis for selection.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant, Sima Liang, Prince of Runan, and the Minister of Works, Wei Guan, also submitted a memorial: "Wei arose after chaos and ruin, when scholars were scattered and thorough vetting was impossible. The nine-rank system was therefore established as a rough, temporary basis for selection.

sentences.zh: 今九域同規，大化方始，臣等以爲宜皆蕩除末法，-{咸}-用土斷，自公卿以下，以所居爲正，無-{復}-縣客，遠屬異土，盡除中正九品之-{制}-，使舉善進-{才}-，各由鄕論，則華競自息，各求-{於}-己矣。」

translations.literal: Now the nine regions are under one rule and great transformation is just beginning. We believe that all the defective laws of the late age should be swept away and territorial registration universally applied.
