From the highest ministers down, one's place of residence should be taken as the standard, with no more registering under distant commanderies or attaching oneself to foreign lands. The Rectifier system and the nine ranks should be entirely abolished, so that recommending the good and advancing talent each proceed from local reputation. Then flashy competition will cease of itself, and each will seek improvement within himself."
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is united under one rule and a great transformation has only just begun. We believe the defective laws of the old regime should all be swept away and household registration tied to the land. From ministers down, residence should determine affiliation—no more distant registration or attachment to foreign commanderies. Abolish the Rectifiers and the nine ranks entirely, let the recommendation of the worthy and the advancement of talent rest on local reputation, and flashy competition will die of itself while each man looks to his own improvement."

sentences.zh: 始平王文學江夏李重上疎，以爲：「九品旣除，宜先開移徙，-{聽}-相-{並}-就，則土斷之實行矣。」

translations.literal: Li Chong, Erudite of the Prince of Shiping's household, from Jiangxia, submitted a memorial, stating: "Once the nine ranks are abolished, migration should first be opened, allowing people to move and settle where they choose; then territorial registration can truly be enforced."
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, Erudite in the household of the Prince of Shiping, from Jiangxia, submitted a memorial arguing: "Once the nine ranks are abolished, migration should be opened first—allowing people to move and settle where they choose—so that territorial registration can truly take effect."

sentences.zh: 帝雖善其言而終不能改也。

translations.literal: Although the emperor approved of their words, in the end he could not reform the system.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved of their counsel but in the end could not bring himself to change the system.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，庚午，大赦。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, on the day gengwu, there was a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, on the day gengwu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 閏月，當陽成侯杜預卒。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Du Yu, Marquis of Dangyang, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Du Yu, Marquis of Dangyang, died.

sentences.zh: 是歳，塞外匈奴胡太阿厚帥部落二萬九千三百人來降，帝處之塞内西河。

translations.literal: In this year, Hu Tai'a-hou of the Xiongnu beyond the frontier led twenty-nine thousand three hundred people of his tribe to surrender, and the emperor settled them within the frontier in Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: That year Hu Tai'a-hou of the Xiongnu beyond the frontier led twenty-nine thousand three hundred tribesmen to surrender, and the emperor settled them inside the frontier in Xihe.

sentences.zh: 罷-{寧}-州入益州，置南夷校尉以護之。

translations.literal: Ning province was abolished and merged into Yi province, and a Commandant of the Southern Yi was appointed to oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: Ning province was abolished and merged into Yi province, and a Commandant of the Southern Yi was appointed to oversee the region.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，尚書左-{僕}-射劉毅致仕，尋卒。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Liu Yi, retired from office and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Liu Yi, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, retired from office and soon died.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以王渾爲尚書左-{僕}-射，渾子濟爲侍中。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Wang Hun was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Hun's son Ji was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuchen, Wang Hun was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and his son Yang Ji was made Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 渾主者處事不當，濟明法繩之。

translations.literal: In the affairs Hun oversaw, matters were handled improperly, and Ji applied the law clearly to restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: In the affairs under Hun's supervision, business was handled improperly, and Ji applied the law strictly to hold him to account.

sentences.zh: 濟從兄佑，素與濟不協，因毀濟不能容其父，帝由是疎濟，-{後}-坐事免官。

translations.literal: Ji's older cousin Hu had long been on bad terms with Ji and therefore slandered him, saying Ji could not tolerate his own father. Because of this the emperor grew distant from Ji, and later Ji was dismissed from office for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's older cousin Yang Hu had long been at odds with him and slandered him, claiming Ji could not even tolerate his own father. The emperor therefore distanced himself from Ji, and Ji was later dismissed from office for an offense.

sentences.zh: 濟性豪侈，帝謂侍中和嶠曰：「我將罵濟而-{後}-官之，如何？」

translations.literal: Ji was by nature extravagant and arrogant. The emperor said to the Attendant-in-Ordinary He Qiao: "I intend to rebuke Ji and then reappoint him—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji was by nature extravagant. The emperor said to the Attendant-in-Ordinary He Qiao, "I plan to scold Ji and then give him office again—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 嶠曰：「濟俊爽，恐不可屈。」

translations.literal: Qiao said: "Ji is brilliant and high-spirited; I fear he cannot be broken."
translations.idiomatic: Qiao replied, "Ji is brilliant and proud—I fear he will not be broken."

sentences.zh: 帝乃召濟，切讓之，旣而曰：「頗知愧不？」

translations.literal: The emperor then summoned Ji and sharply reproved him, then said: "Do you feel any shame at all?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then summoned Ji and rebuked him sharply, then asked, "Do you feel any shame?"

sentences.zh: 濟曰：「『尺布』、『-{斗}-粟』之謠，常爲陛下愧之。

translations.literal: Ji said: "The ballad of 'a foot of cloth' and 'a peck of grain'—I am always ashamed on Your Majesty's account because of it.
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "The ballad of 'a foot of cloth, a peck of grain'—I am always ashamed on Your Majesty's account because of it.

sentences.zh: 他人能令親者疎，臣不能令親者親，以此愧陛下耳。」

translations.literal: Others can make kin grow distant; I cannot make kin grow close. It is for this that I am ashamed before Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Others can drive kin apart; I cannot make kin draw close. That is why I am ashamed before Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 嶠，治之孫也。

translations.literal: Qiao was the grandson of He Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao was the grandson of He Zhi.

sentences.zh: 靑、梁、幽、冀州旱。

translations.literal: Qing, Liang, You, and Ji provinces suffered drought.
translations.idiomatic: Qing, Liang, You, and Ji provinces suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，丙戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on the first day of the cycle (bingxu), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on the new moon of the day bingxu, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，庚子，襄陽武侯王濬卒。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, on the day gengzi, Wang Jun, Marquis of Xiangyang, died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, on the day gengzi, Wang Jun, Marquis of Xiangyang, died.

sentences.zh: 是歳，慕容刪爲其下所殺，部衆-{復}-迎渉歸子廆而立之。

translations.literal: In this year, Murong Shan was killed by his subordinates, and the tribesmen again welcomed Shegui's son Hui and established him as leader.
translations.idiomatic: That year Murong Shan was killed by his own followers, and the tribesmen again welcomed Shegui's son Murong Hui and installed him as leader.

sentences.zh: 渉歸與宇文部素有隙，廆請討之，朝廷弗許。

translations.literal: Shegui had long been at odds with the Yuwen tribe, and Hui requested permission to attack them, but the court did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Shegui had long been at odds with the Yuwen tribe, and Hui requested permission to attack them, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 廆怒，入寇遼西，殺略甚衆。

translations.literal: Hui grew angry, invaded Liaoxi, and killed and plundered a great many people.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Hui raided Liaoxi, killing and plundering on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 帝遣幽州軍討廆，戰-{於}-肥如，廆衆大敗。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched the army of You province to attack Hui. They fought at Feiru, and Hui's forces were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the army of You province against Hui. At Feiru they gave battle, and Hui's forces were routed.

sentences.zh: 自是毎歳犯邊，又東撃扶-{餘}-，扶-{餘}-王依慮自殺；

translations.literal: From then on he raided the frontier every year. He also attacked Fuyu to the east, and the king of Fuyu, Yilu, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he raided the frontier every year. He also struck east against Fuyu, and the king of Fuyu, Yilu, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 子弟走保沃沮。

translations.literal: His sons and younger brothers fled to take refuge in Woju.
translations.idiomatic: His sons and younger brothers fled for safety to Woju.

sentences.zh: 廆夷其國城，驅萬-{餘}-人而歸。

translations.literal: Hui destroyed the capital of their state and drove more than ten thousand people back with him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui razed the Fuyu capital and drove more than ten thousand captives home with him.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲寅朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day of the cycle (jiayin), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of the day jiayin, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 魏舒稱疾，固請遜位，以劇陽子罷。

translations.literal: Wei Shu claimed illness and firmly requested to yield his position; Liu Ba, Marquis of Juyang, replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu pleaded illness and firmly asked to step down; Liu Ba, Marquis of Juyang, replaced him.

sentences.zh: 舒所爲，必先行而-{後}-言，遜位之際，莫有知者。

translations.literal: In whatever Shu did, he always acted first and spoke afterward. At the moment he yielded his position, no one knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: In whatever Shu undertook, he always acted first and spoke afterward. When he stepped down, no one had known it was coming.

sentences.zh: 衞瓘與舒書曰：「毎與足下共論此事，日日未果，可謂『瞻之在前，忽焉在-{後}-』矣。」

translations.literal: Wei Guan wrote to Shu, saying: "Every time I discussed this matter with you, day after day it came to nothing. One might say, 'It seemed right before my eyes, yet suddenly it was behind me.'"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan wrote to Shu: "Every time you and I discussed this, day after day nothing came of it. One might say, 'It seemed right before my eyes, yet suddenly it was behind me.'"

sentences.zh: 夏，慕容廆寇遼東，故扶-{餘}-王依慮子依羅求帥見人還-{復}-舊國，請援-{於}-東夷校尉何龕，龕遣督護賈沈將兵送之。

translations.literal: In summer, Murong Hui raided Liaodong. Yiluo, son of the former king of Fuyu, Yilu, requested troops to lead his people back and restore the old state. He asked aid from He Kan, Commandant of the Eastern Yi, and Kan dispatched the Supervisor Jia Shen with troops to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer Murong Hui raided Liaodong. Yiluo, son of the former king of Fuyu, Yilu, asked for troops to lead his people home and restore their kingdom. He sought help from He Kan, Commandant of the Eastern Yi, who dispatched the Supervisor Jia Shen with an escort.

sentences.zh: 廆遣其將孫丁帥騎邀之-{於}-路，沈力戰，斬丁，遂-{復}-扶-{餘}-。

translations.literal: Hui sent his general Sun Ding at the head of cavalry to intercept them on the road. Shen fought fiercely, beheaded Ding, and thus restored Fuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Hui sent his general Sun Ding with cavalry to intercept them on the road. Shen fought hard, killed Ding, and restored Fuyu.

sentences.zh: 秋，匈奴胡都大博及萎莎胡各帥-{種}-落十萬-{餘}-口詣雍州降。

translations.literal: In autumn, Hu Dudu Bo of the Xiongnu and the chiefs of the Weisha Hu each led more than one hundred thousand people of their tribes to surrender at Yong province.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn Hu Dudu Bo of the Xiongnu and the chiefs of the Weisha Hu each led more than one hundred thousand tribesmen to surrender at Yong province.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊寅，扶風武王駿薨。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day wuyin, Prince Wu of Fufeng, Jun, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day wuyin, Prince Wu of Fufeng, Sima Jun, died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，壬子，以隴西王泰都督關中諸軍事。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day renzi, Sima Tai, Prince of Longxi, was made commander over all military affairs in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day renzi, Sima Tai, Prince of Longxi, was appointed commander over all military affairs in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 泰，宣帝弟馗之子也。

translations.literal: Tai was the son of Kui, younger brother of Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was the son of Kui, younger brother of Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 是歳，鮮卑拓跋悉鹿卒，弟綽立。

translations.literal: In this year, Tuoba Xilu of the Xianbei died, and his younger brother Chuo succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: That year Tuoba Xilu of the Xianbei died, and his younger brother Chuo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊申朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day of the cycle (wushen), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of the day wushen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 太廟殿陷，秋，九月，改營太廟，作者六萬人。

translations.literal: The hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple collapsed; in autumn, in the ninth month, the temple was rebuilt, with sixty thousand laborers employed.
translations.idiomatic: The hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple collapsed. In autumn, in the ninth month, the temple was rebuilt with sixty thousand laborers.

sentences.zh: 是歳，匈奴都督大豆得一育鞠等-{復}-帥-{種}-落萬一千五百口來降。

translations.literal: This year, Dadou Deyu Ju and others, Xiongnu commanders, again led tribes totaling 11,500 persons to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: This year Dadou Deyu Ju and other Xiongnu commanders again led tribes totaling 11,500 persons to surrender.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬申朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on renshen, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on renshen, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，庚子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, in the sixth month, on gengzi, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the sixth month, on gengzi, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 郡國三十三大旱。

translations.literal: Thirty-three commanderies and kingdoms suffered severe drought.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-three commanderies and kingdoms suffered severe drought.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，壬子；

translations.literal: In autumn, in the eighth month, on renzi;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, on renzi;

sentences.zh: 星隕如雨。

translations.literal: stars fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: stars fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 地震。

translations.literal: There was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: There was an earthquake.
